```html
  </div>
  <dialog id="role-dialog" data-dialog aria-labelledby="role-dialog-title">
    <header>
      <h2 id="role-dialog-title">Level 4: dialog</h2>
    </header>
    <p>The highest level, with the lightest surface in the dark scheme.</p>
    <form method="dialog">
      <footer>
        <button type="submit" autofocus>Close</button>
      </footer>
    </form>
  </dialog>
  <dui-toaster data-alert="toasts" role="status"></dui-toaster>
</div>
```

## Opinions we hold

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/opinions-we-hold.html

Each of these is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** [logical properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values)
  (`margin-block`, `inline-size`), so right-to-left and vertical writing modes work unchanged.
- **Our choice:** keep link underlines, because color alone is not enough to spot a link (WCAG 1.4.1).
- **Our choice:** system font stacks from [Modern Font Stacks](https://modernfontstacks.com/),
  because they cost no network requests and match the platform.
- **Our choice:** a fluid type scale with [`clamp()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/clamp)
  in `rem`, so text grows with the viewport and still respects the user's font size.
- **Our choice:** a 65ch measure for prose, near the commonly cited 45 to 75 characters per line
  ([WCAG 1.4.8 Visual Presentation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/visual-presentation.html) asks for 80 or fewer).
- **Our choice:** rhythm from the "lobotomized owl" selector (`* + *`) inside flow containers
  ([Heydon Pickering](https://alistapart.com/article/axiomatic-css-and-lobotomized-owls/)), wrapped in
  `:where()` so it has zero specificity.
- **Our choice:** `type="submit"` buttons get the accent fill and other buttons stay neutral,
  so the primary action is marked by its native type, with no class.
- **Our choice:** checkboxes, radios and range keep native rendering tinted with
  [`accent-color`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/accent-color), because
  native controls keep their platform accessibility.
- **Our choice:** each atom has one `data-<atom>` attribute whose value is a space-separated
  list (`data-button="primary small"`), matched with `~=`, instead of modifier classes. The
  other atom choices (button variants, focus rings, switch, field errors, badge tints) are
  listed with their reasons in the [atoms index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md#our-choices).
- **Our choice:** molecules follow the same rule (`data-card="link"`, `data-dialog="drawer end"`),
  or use the native element or ARIA role when that already says everything (`<search>`,
  `role="toolbar"`). The molecule choices are listed with their reasons in the
  [molecules index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md#our-choices); the main ones:
  - **Our choice:** tabs select on focus (automatic activation), as the
    [APG recommends](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus)
    when panels show at once; `activation="manual"` is available.
  - **Our choice:** the drawer is a `<dialog>` variant, so the browser handles modality, focus and
    <kbd>Esc</kbd> ([explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/drawer.md)).
  - **Our choice:** a clickable card links its heading and stretches that link over the card, so the
    accessible name stays the heading ([explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/card.md)).
  - **Our choice:** toasts never dismiss themselves and never take focus ([explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/toast.md)).
  - **Our choice:** the typeahead (`<dui-combobox>`) upgrades a native `<input list>` + `<datalist>`, not a
    `<select>`, because the value is free text and the upgrade reuses the same input and options. It
    follows the [APG Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) list autocomplete
    variant, filters by "contains" like the native
    [`<datalist>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/datalist) popups
    in Chromium and Firefox, and positions its listbox under the input rather than in the top layer, so
    it is never wider than the field ([explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/combobox.md)).
- **Our choice:** organisms (page header, filter bar, form sections, data table) follow the same one-attribute rule
  (`data-page-header`, `data-filter-bar`, `data-form-sections`, `data-table`) and take the rest of their layout from their
  children's native elements. Their choices are listed in the
  [organisms index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/organisms/README.md#our-choices); the main ones:
  - **Our choice:** the filter bar is a `<form method="get">` in `<search>` with an Apply button and a
    `role="status"` result count present from page load, so filters live in the URL, work without
    JavaScript and are announced ([4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)).
  - **Our choice:** form sections are headed `<section>` elements with a `<header>` and one body of fields,
    not fieldsets, because a `<legend>` cannot be placed in a grid column; related controls still go in a
    `<fieldset>` inside the body.
  - **Our choice:** the data table (`data-table` on a native `<table>`) has sortable headers that are plain
    text in the markup; `<dui-table>` turns them into buttons and follows the
    [APG Sortable Table](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/examples/sortable-table/) example
    (`aria-sort` on the sorted header only, a visually hidden caption hint, nothing else announced), so with
    JavaScript off there are no buttons that do nothing. A selected row shows a checked checkbox, a bar on its
    leading edge and a tint, never color alone; the count is a `role="status"` element present from load.
  - **Our choice:** a sticky table header sticks to the nearest scroll container, so a sticky table goes in
    `data-scroll="block inline"` (at most `--dui-size-pane` tall) or in none; numeric columns are marked per
    cell with the same attribute (`data-table="number"`), because words on the table cannot target a column.
- **Our choice:** layout primitives come from [Every Layout](https://every-layout.dev/)'s
  Stack, Cluster and Grid. Their custom properties are registered with
  [`@property`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property) as non-inheriting,
  so a nested primitive keeps its own default.

### Links: visited state

[`:visited`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:visited) tells a reader which
destinations they have already seen. WCAG does not require it:
[Understanding 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html) says conveying a
link's visited status "is not an author responsibility". The visited color still meets 4.5:1.

- **Our choice:** only content links take `--dui-color-link-visited`. Navigational links keep their
  unvisited color, because a reader picks a destination again on every page and "seen before" is noise
  there. Navigational means: inside a [`<nav>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
  or `role="navigation"`, `menu`, `menubar`, `tablist` or `toolbar`; a `role="tab"` or `menuitem*` link;
  a link with `data-button`; or a same-page `#fragment` link (skip links, tables of contents).
- The base rule does this with `a:visited:not(:where(…))`, so it stays at the specificity of `a:visited`
  and needs no per-component resets. In forced colors, navigational links show `LinkText` and content
  links show `VisitedText`.
- **Either way:** mark a navigational link outside a `<nav>` with `data-link="nav"` (combines with
  `quiet`) to drop the visited color. For the rare content link inside a `<nav>`, set
  `color: var(--dui-color-link-visited)` on its `:visited` state in your own CSS, which beats the layers.

### Icons

- **Our choice:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) is the icon set, because its SVGs already use our 24px grid, 2px round
  `currentColor` stroke and need no build. Credit: Lucide is under the [ISC licence](https://lucide.dev/license); the
  icons it took from [Feather](https://github.com/feathericons/feather) are under the
  [MIT licence](https://github.com/feathericons/feather/blob/main/LICENSE). [Tabler](https://tabler.io/icons) and
  [Heroicons](https://heroicons.com) were the alternatives considered.
- **Our choice:** icons are inline SVG, copied from the official set into the markup. The repository ships no icon
  files, sprite, font or package. The recipe: copy the icon from lucide.dev, replace its `class` with
  [`data-icon`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/icon.md), add `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"`, keep everything else
  (`viewBox`, `fill="none"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, `width` and `height`) as Lucide ships it, and note the icon's name
  in a comment. `data-icon` sizes it to `--dui-size-icon` and keeps it from shrinking; the stroke follows the text color
  through [`currentColor`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value#currentcolor), so it follows
  themes and [forced colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors) with no extra CSS.

  [`examples/atoms/icon.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/icon.md) shows the recipe in every context.

- **Decorative or meaningful.** An icon beside a visible label is decoration: `aria-hidden="true"`, so the label is the
  name and is not announced twice ([1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html)).
  A standalone icon that carries meaning, outside a control, is `role="img"` with a `<title>` (and `aria-labelledby`
  pointing at it). In a control, the name goes on the control, never on the SVG
  ([4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html),
  [APG: names and descriptions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/)).
- **Contrast.** An icon that is the only sign of a control or a state meets 3:1
  ([1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)); a selected state
  changes the drawing (filled or outlined), not only its color.
- **Our choice:** icon plus a visible label is the default. Label only is always fine, and better when no icon comes to
  mind at once. If the label is visible, the accessible name contains it
  ([2.5.3 Label in Name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html)).
- **Our choice:** icon only (`data-button="icon"`) is allowed only for these widely recognized actions: search, close,
  open or close navigation (menu), play, pause, stop, skip, expand and collapse, back, forward, edit, more (overflow),
  settings in an app bar, and add item in a dense toolbar. A product-specific metaphor is never icon only. The button
  - is named for the action ("Search", "Close"), never the picture ("Magnifying glass", "X"), with visually hidden text
    inside it;
  - shows a visible tooltip with the same words on hover **and** keyboard focus, which <kbd>Esc</kbd> hides and the
    pointer can move onto ([1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html)).
    The tooltip is `<dui-tooltip>` with a `popover="hint"`: no browser can show a popover on hover and focus without
    script except Chromium, through [`interestfor`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/button#interestfor),
    which Firefox and Safari do not support yet;
  - is a square of `--dui-size-control` (32px compact, 44px comfortable), never smaller than 24 by 24 pixels
    ([2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).
- **Our choice:** no icon-only destructive actions. Delete, remove, empty and reset always show their word; a trash icon
  may sit beside it. For that reason delete is not on the list above, even in a toolbar.
- **Our choice:** navigation keeps visible text. Icons in nav links and app bar buttons are decoration.
- **Our choice:** in right-to-left text, flip only icons whose meaning has a direction, with `data-icon="mirror"`
  (flipped under [`:dir(rtl)`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:dir), which follows the nearest `dir`
  attribute): arrows, chevrons, back and forward, undo and redo, indent and outdent, text alignment to the start or end.
  Never flip search, close, play, check, clocks or logos.
- **Icon fonts are rejected.** A ligature or private-use glyph is text: user text spacing
  ([1.4.12 Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing.html)) can break the ligature into
  words, a font that fails to load shows letters or empty boxes, and screen readers may read the ligature name.

## Layout primitives

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/layout-primitives.html

| Class | What it does | Custom properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.stack` | Vertical flow with a gap | `--stack-gap` |
| `.cluster` | Wrapping inline group | `--cluster-gap`, `--cluster-justify`, `--cluster-align` |
| `.grid` | Auto-fit responsive grid, no media queries | `--grid-min`, `--grid-gap` |
| `[data-scroll="inline"]` | Scroll container for content wider than the screen, such as a data table | None |
| `[data-scroll="block inline"]` | Also scrolls vertically, at most `--dui-size-pane` (the viewport) tall, so a sticky table header stays in view | None |

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 12rem">…</div>
```

On a `ul` or `ol`, the primitive also removes list markers and padding.

### Page layouts

Larger layouts for application screens, each one attribute on a wrapper, live in `css/layout/` too and
are shown in [`examples/layouts/`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md):

| Attribute | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `data-list-detail` | A list of links (`aria-current` on the selected one) beside a labelled detail; the detail scrolls on its own when side by side |
| `data-split="[1:1 \| 1:2 \| 2:1]"` | Two regions side by side at a ratio |
| `data-dashboard`, `data-dashboard="wide \| full"` on a tile | Headed tiles on raised surfaces that reflow without media queries |
| `data-action-bar` | A form's buttons in a bar that sticks to the bottom of the scroll area and never hides the focused field |
| `data-app-shell`, `data-app-shell="contained"` | The frame of an application: `<header>`, a primary sidebar (`<nav>`), `<main>`, an optional auxiliary `<aside>` and `<footer>` in named grid areas; `<dui-app-shell>` makes the sidebars collapsible and drawers when narrow |

Each one is side by side when its wrapper is wide and stacked when it is narrow, from 320px up, and keeps
source order (the reading and Tab order) in both. A settings page needs no API of its own: it is a
`data-list-detail` of in-page links beside `data-form-sections` with a `data-action-bar`
([example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md)).

- **Our choice:** layouts and [organisms](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/organisms/README.md) switch with a
  [container query](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Containment/Container_queries)
  on their own wrapper, not a media query, because they sit in regions of any width: a page, a split, the
  main area of an app shell. Media queries are kept for decisions about the whole viewport. A container
  query condition cannot read a custom property, so each breakpoint is a length written in the file header.
- **Our choice:** list-detail items are links to the item's own URL, not buttons that swap content, so
  history, bookmarks and the no-JavaScript case work.
- **Our choice:** the sticky action bar reserves its height as `scroll-padding-block-end` on every ancestor
  of its form, so whichever one scrolls keeps the focused field clear of the bar
  ([2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html),
  technique [C43](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C43)).
- **Our choice:** the app shell is the landmarks HTML already has, in source order, placed with
  `grid-template-areas`; parts are recognized by element and position, so none needs an attribute
  ([APG Landmark Regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/),
  [explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md)). Without JavaScript both sidebars are always shown (stacked when narrow)
  and the toggles stay `hidden`, so no button does nothing.
- **Our choice:** one copy of each sidebar. Beside main it is a plain landmark that its toggle hides with
  `hidden`; on a narrow shell `<dui-app-shell>` moves the same element into a modal drawer `<dialog>` while the
  drawer is open, so screen readers hear "dialog" only while it is one and the navigation is never duplicated.
- **Our choice:** the shell switches on its own width (container queries at 48rem for the primary sidebar
  and 64rem for the auxiliary one, and a `ResizeObserver` in the element), and `<main>` and each sidebar are
  named size containers, so a contained shell works anywhere and the layouts inside main follow main's width.
- **Our choice:** the sidebar navigation is the nav molecule (`data-nav="vertical"`) with optional decorative
  icons, not a tree view: an [APG Tree View](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/) is for
  hierarchies users navigate as data (file trees) with roving focus and arrow keys; site navigation is links,
  so disclosure groups and links ([APG Disclosure Navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/))
  are the right semantics.
- **Our choice:** the selected item of a list-detail is marked like a selected table row: a
  `--dui-border-width-emphasis` bar on its leading edge, a tint and bold text, with the bar drawn in
  `Highlight` in forced colors mode ([1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html),
  [1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)).
- **Our choice:** splits have a fixed ratio and no draggable divider; a resizable one would follow the
  [APG Window Splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) pattern
  ([explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/split-view.md)).

Wrap any table that may not fit a 320px screen in `data-scroll="inline"`, named by its caption:

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="orders-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-caption">Recent orders</caption>
    …
  </table>
</section>
```

`tabindex="0"` makes it scrollable from the keyboard
([2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html), axe
[`scrollable-region-focusable`](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable)),
and a named `<section>` is a [region landmark](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section), so
screen reader users hear what that focus stop is. **Our choice:** `<section>` rather than
`<div role="region">`, because the native element already has the role. Data tables
may scroll sideways under [1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html);
the page itself must not. Never set `display: block` on the `<table>` instead: it can drop table
semantics in some browsers ([Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html)).
A `<pre>` already scrolls (`overflow-x: auto`); authors MUST give every `<pre>` (and any
`data-scroll="inline"` container) `tabindex="0"` so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.

## Web components

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/web-components.html

HTML still has no element for tabs, menus, roving focus in a toolbar, hover tooltips or a toast
stack. For those, and only those, [`web-components/`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/web-components.md) has one small
custom element each: `<dui-tabs>`, `<dui-menu>`, `<dui-combobox>`, `<dui-toolbar>`, `<dui-tooltip>`,
`<dui-toaster>`, `<dui-table>` (sorting rows and selecting them, which a `<table>` cannot do) and `<dui-app-shell>`
(collapsing sidebars and turning them into modal drawers on a narrow shell, which a button cannot do by itself). HTML does have `<datalist>`, but its popup cannot be styled and differs between engines,
so `<dui-combobox>` upgrades it to a listbox the page owns.

- **Light DOM.** No shadow root: the molecule CSS and your CSS style the markup directly.
- **Progressive enhancement.** The markup works before the script runs and with JavaScript off:
  tabs are a `<nav>` of in-page links and headed sections, toolbar buttons are Tab stops, a menu's
  popover still opens, a tooltip is still the button's description, a data table keeps the server's order
  with plain-text headers and ordinary checkboxes, an app shell shows both sidebars and no toggles.
- **ARIA with behavior, or not at all.** An element adds roles such as `menu` or `tab` only together
  with the keyboard support those roles promise ([APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)).
- **Why each exists** is written at the top of its file, and the
  [web components index](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/web-components.md) lists them. Each one is a plain ES module with no
  dependencies and no build: `<script type="module" src="web-components/dui-tabs.js"></script>`.

## Explainers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/explainers.html

A pattern with no native element and no APG pattern is written up like a platform proposal in
[`explainers/`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/index.md): problem, use cases, goals and non-goals, markup and API,
keyboard, accessibility mappings, alternatives, prior art and open questions, with normative
text in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) keywords. The card, pagination, drawer
and toast molecules have one, and so do density, the combobox, the split view, the app shell and
its auxiliary sidebar, which record the choices their
standards leave open. Names follow HTML and ARIA conventions, so a pattern could map onto
a future native element or attribute.

## Tooling

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/tooling.html

`npm test` runs, in order, and fails if any step fails:

| Script | Tool | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lint:html` | [html-validate](https://html-validate.org/) | `examples/**/*.html` against `html-validate:recommended` |
| `lint:css` | [Stylelint](https://stylelint.io/) | `css/**/*.css` against `stylelint-config-standard` |
| `lint:tokens` | `scripts/check-tokens.mjs` | Semantic-only tokens and no literal colors or sizes outside `css/tokens/` |
| `test:a11y` | [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) + [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) | Every `examples/**/*.html` (atoms and molecules included) in light and dark, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`, including open dialogs and drawers, open popovers and menus, shown tooltips and toasts, every tab selected and every details expanded; no horizontal page overflow and no axe violations at 320×640 and 375×812; no external requests; token contrast pairs (atoms and molecules included) in the default and forest themes; rendered focus-ring and indicator contrast; atom and molecule states through accessibility APIs; molecule keyboard behavior against the APG; no-JavaScript fallbacks; fallbacks for engine-specific features; scoped theming of atoms and molecules; layouts and organisms side by side when wide and stacked when narrow, the sticky action bar never covering the focused field, data table sorting, selection, sticky header and loading state (with and without JavaScript), and 24px targets in compact density; the app shell's landmarks and grid areas, collapse when wide, modal drawers with focus return when narrow, one copy of each sidebar, no-JavaScript fallbacks and axe with the drawers open |

Preview locally with `npm run serve` (a zero-dependency static server) and open
<http://127.0.0.1:4173/examples/base.html>. To run tests from two checkouts at once, give each its own port, e.g. `PORT=4273 npm test`.

Rule relaxations, each with its reason:

- **Stylelint `custom-property-pattern`** is replaced, not disabled. The standard kebab-case
  pattern rejects `--dui-step--1` (the double hyphen marks a negative step, a common naming for
  type scales below zero). The replacement still requires kebab-case and only allows names
  starting with `--dui-` or the documented layout properties (`--stack-*`, `--cluster-*`, `--grid-*`).
- **Engine-specific test**: the field test also reads the `invalid` state from the accessibility
  tree through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, which only Chromium offers; Firefox and WebKit run the
  rest of that test (attribute and accessible description). The molecule tests do the same for the
  expanded state of `<summary>` and of a `popovertarget` button, which browsers expose natively but
  Playwright's role engine does not compute; the other engines check the `open` attribute and the
  popover's visibility instead. No browser is skipped.
- **Feature fallbacks**: where every engine in the test run supports a feature (anchor positioning,
  `@starting-style`, `closedby`, `popover="hint"`), the molecule tests also exercise the fallback path
  by removing the feature in the page: deleting the `@supports` or `@starting-style` rules from the
  CSSOM, removing the `closedby` attribute, or setting `popover="manual"` (what `hint` falls back to).
- **Settling transitions**: axe and geometry checks wait for running CSS transitions to finish, so they
  measure final colors and positions rather than a frame mid-fade.
- **External-request check**: same-origin `blob:` URLs are allowed, because WebKit routes these
  in-memory objects through the request handler. Any other origin still fails the test.
- **html-validate**: none. `html-validate:recommended` is used as-is. Inline `style` attributes
  that set only custom properties are already allowed by its
  [`no-inline-style`](https://html-validate.org/rules/no-inline-style.html) default
  (`allowVariables: true`), which is how the layout primitives are configured.

## Edges and alignment

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/edges-and-alignment.html

**Our choice:** every container has a few named vertical lines, written in tokens, and every item sits on one of them
or has a written reason, because edges picked by eye drift by a few pixels per panel and nobody can say which was meant.
No web standard covers this. The method is prior art, not a spec: Karri Saarinen's redraw of the Linear sidebar
([How we redesigned the Linear UI](https://linear.app/now/how-we-redesigned-the-linear-ui)) and the
[Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout),
as packaged by the [gridlines](https://github.com/pritamux/gridlines) skill. Standards win any conflict:
[2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html), focus outlines
and forced-colors borders are never reduced to close a gap; the gap is left and written down.

- **Box line and text line.** Boxed rows and controls (nav links, menu items, list rows, tabs, table rows, buttons)
  put their box on the container's content edge and their label one control padding in. **Our choice:** the box never
  hangs outside its container (the skill's "pull the strip in" for tabs), because a hit area or focus ring past the
  edge is clipped by scroll containers and goes off screen in a container with no padding.
- **Icons on one column, labels on one line.** In a list, every row's icon starts on the same column and every
  label on the same line, whatever sits before them (an indicator bar, a disclosure marker).
- **Bars centre on one line.** Items in a toolbar, app bar, dialog header or page header title row are centred on one
  horizontal line (`align-items: center`); the first item starts on the box line, the last ends on the trailing line.
- Lines use `--dui-space-*` and the other semantic tokens with logical properties (`padding-inline-start`), never px.
  A line that needs a value off the scale means the container's padding is wrong.

The lines, measured from each container's inline-start edge (the trailing line mirrors the leading one unless noted):

| Container | Box line | Text line | Other lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| App shell frame: `<header>`, sidebars, `<footer>` | `--dui-space-m` | box line + the control's `--dui-space-button-inline` (app bar), or the nav's lines below | Trailing: `--dui-space-m`. Each frame region measures from its own edge |
| App shell `<main>` | `--dui-space-l` beside a sidebar, `--dui-space-m` stacked | same as box line | |
| Nav list (`data-nav="vertical"`) | the list's edge; a group's links `--dui-space-m` in | `--dui-border-width-indicator` + `--dui-space-control-inline`, plus `--dui-space-m` for links beside a group (the disclosure marker's width) and inside one | Icon column: starts on the text line, `--dui-size-icon` wide, then `--dui-space-gap` to the label |
| Toolbar (`role="toolbar"`) | `--dui-border-width` + `--dui-space-gap-tight` | box line + `--dui-space-button-inline` | One centre line |
| Menus and popovers | menu items: `--dui-border-width` + `--dui-space-gap-tight` | `--dui-border-width` + `--dui-space-m` (a menu: `--dui-space-gap-tight` + `--dui-space-control-inline`, equal at comfortable density) | A horizontal nav's dropdown adds its `--dui-border-width-indicator` |
| Tabs | the tab list's edge | box line + `--dui-space-button-inline` | Panel text on the tab list's edge |
| Dialogs and drawers | `--dui-border-width` + `--dui-space-l` | same as box line | Header title and close button share a centre line; footer actions end on the trailing line |
| List-detail | list rows on the list's edge | rows: `--dui-border-width-emphasis` + `--dui-space-control-inline`; detail: `--dui-focus-width` + `--dui-focus-offset` side by side (room for focus rings), its edge when stacked | |
| Data table | rows on the table's edge; the caption on it too | `--dui-space-cell` | Checkbox column: one centre line; body rows' `--dui-border-width-emphasis` bar is matched by the header cell's padding. Number columns end on `--dui-space-cell` |
| Page header (`data-page-header`) | the region's edge | same as box line | Actions end on the trailing line (the edge); title and actions share a centre line |

These were read from the CSS in an alignment pass on 21 November 2026 (Owen Donckers, with Claude), taking the line
most rows already used. [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/contributing.md#alignment-passes) explains how to run a pass.

## Primitive tokens

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/primitives.html

**Internal.** Raw values named by what they are, not by what they are for. Only [`css/tokens/semantic.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md) may reference these. Base, layout, utility and component CSS must use semantic tokens instead; `npm run lint:tokens` enforces this.

Primitives are NOT public API: they may be renamed, added or removed in any release. Theme with semantic tokens.

Colors are OKLCH, in the sRGB gamut (CSS Color 4). [W3C ok lab](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#ok-lab) [MDN `oklch`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/color_value/oklch)

Neutral and indigo each have 12 steps in light and in dark. The step number is the role, the same idea as Radix's scales (for comparison: 1 page, 2 raised, 3 sunken or element, 4 hover, 5 active or selected, 6 subtle border, 7 border, 8 control border, 9 solid, 10 solid hover, 11 muted or accent text, 12 text. Red, green, amber and blue have steps 3, 9 and 11 only. Purple, teal and yellow keep the code-highlight and mark hues. Our choice: the primary action uses neutral 12 (near-black or near-white), and indigo is the accent for links, focus and selection. ([radix-ui.com understanding the scale](https://www.radix-ui.com/colors/docs/palette-composition/understanding-the-scale))

[Custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*).

167 tokens in [`css/tokens/primitives.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/tokens/primitives.css). **Light** and **Dark** resolve every `var()` and take one side of [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark). Previews are decorative.

### Neutral, light. Hue 265

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-color-neutral-1` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | Step 1, page |
| `--dui-color-neutral-2` | `oklch(98.2% 0.003 265deg)` | `oklch(98.2% 0.003 265deg)` | Step 2, raised |
| `--dui-color-neutral-3` | `oklch(96.2% 0.005 265deg)` | `oklch(96.2% 0.005 265deg)` | Step 3, sunken or element |
| `--dui-color-neutral-4` | `oklch(94% 0.006 265deg)` | `oklch(94% 0.006 265deg)` | Step 4, hover |
| `--dui-color-neutral-5` | `oklch(91% 0.008 265deg)` | `oklch(91% 0.008 265deg)` | Step 5, active or selected |
| `--dui-color-neutral-6` | `oklch(84% 0.01 265deg)` | `oklch(84% 0.01 265deg)` | Step 6, subtle border |
| `--dui-color-neutral-7` | `oklch(72% 0.013 265deg)` | `oklch(72% 0.013 265deg)` | Step 7, border |
| `--dui-color-neutral-8` | `oklch(58.5% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(58.5% 0.016 265deg)` | Step 8, control border, 3:1 on the page |
| `--dui-color-neutral-9` | `oklch(52% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(52% 0.016 265deg)` | Step 9, solid |
| `--dui-color-neutral-10` | `oklch(50% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(50% 0.016 265deg)` | Step 10, solid hover |
| `--dui-color-neutral-11` | `oklch(47.5% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(47.5% 0.016 265deg)` | Step 11, muted text |
| `--dui-color-neutral-12` | `oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg)` | `oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg)` | Step 12, text, and the light primary fill |
| `--dui-color-neutral-12-a11` | `oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%)` | `oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%)` | Hairline: the text color at 11% alpha |
| `--dui-color-neutral-punctuation` | `oklch(37% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(37% 0.016 265deg)` | Code punctuation, darker than muted text |
| `--dui-color-neutral-shadow` | `oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%)` | `oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%)` | Shadow tinted with the neutral hue |

### Neutral, dark. Hue 265. Lightness rises with the step

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Shadow geometry

X offset, y offset, blur, spread. The color is added by the semantic elevation tokens. Each level is a 1px ring plus one or two layers with a negative spread, so the shadow stays tucked under the edge and reads as a crisp lift rather than a smudge. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/box-shadow> For comparison: Radix Themes shadows (a 1px ring plus layers, <https://www.radix-ui.com/themes/docs/theme/shadows>) and Tailwind v4 (negative spread, <https://tailwindcss.com/docs/box-shadow>).

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-shadow-ring` | `0 0 0 1px` | `0 0 0 1px` | The 1px ring every elevated role draws in the hairline color |
| `--dui-shadow-highlight` | `inset 0 1px 0 0` | `inset 0 1px 0 0` | Dark scheme: a 1px top highlight on levels 2 to 4 |
| `--dui-shadow-1-key` | `0 1px 2px -1px` | `0 1px 2px -1px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-2-key` | `0 2px 4px -2px` | `0 2px 4px -2px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-2-ambient` | `0 4px 12px -4px` | `0 4px 12px -4px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-3-key` | `0 4px 8px -4px` | `0 4px 8px -4px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-3-ambient` | `0 12px 24px -8px` | `0 12px 24px -8px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-4-key` | `0 8px 16px -8px` | `0 8px 16px -8px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-4-ambient` | `0 24px 48px -12px` | `0 24px 48px -12px` | No description yet. |
| `--dui-shadow-none` | `none` | `none` | No shadow |

## Semantic tokens

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.html

**Public theming API.** Named by role. Each points at a primitive ([`css/tokens/primitives.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/primitives.md)) or at another semantic token. Base, layout, utility and component CSS use only these. Renaming or removing one is a breaking change.

A theme is an override of these tokens on `:root` or on a scoped element. No rebuild. See [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md).

Colors use [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark), which picks a value from the used color-scheme of the element where the token is read.

146 tokens in [`css/tokens/semantic.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/tokens/semantic.css). **Light** and **Dark** resolve every `var()` and take one side of [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark). Previews are decorative. † marks a description taken from the semantic token table in [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md).

### Surfaces and text

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-color-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg)` | Page background |
| `--dui-color-surface-raised` | `oklch(98.2% 0.003 265deg)` | `oklch(19% 0.007 265deg)` | Slightly lifted areas: neutral buttons, zebra rows, cards |
| `--dui-color-surface-sunken` | `oklch(96.2% 0.005 265deg)` | `oklch(22% 0.009 265deg)` | Recessed areas: code, button hover |
| `--dui-color-text` | `oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg)` | `oklch(95% 0.004 265deg)` | Body text |
| `--dui-color-text-muted` | `oklch(47.5% 0.016 265deg)` | `oklch(76% 0.012 265deg)` | Secondary text, still 4.5:1 |

### Motion knobs

Durations and distances (section 2) are derived from these.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-motion-scale` | `1` | `1` | Multiplies every motion duration: 2 is twice as slow, 0 turns motion off |
| `--dui-motion-movement` | `1` | `1` | 1 lets things slide, lift and zoom; 0 (reduced motion) keeps fades and color changes only With `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: `var(--dui-factor-0)`, resolves to `0`. With `[data-motion="reduced"]`: `var(--dui-factor-0)`, resolves to `0`. With `[data-motion="none"]`: `var(--dui-factor-0)`, resolves to `0`. |
| `--dui-motion-enabled` | `1` | `1` | 0 (data-motion="none") makes every duration 0s, whatever the scale set inside With `[data-motion="none"]`: `var(--dui-factor-0)`, resolves to `0`. |
| `--dui-motion-easing-standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Easing for state changes that stay on screen: hover, press, switch |
| `--dui-motion-easing-enter` | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1)` | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1)` | Easing for things arriving: dialogs, drawers, popovers, toasts |
| `--dui-motion-easing-exit` | `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1)` | `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1)` | Easing for things leaving |

### Motion

Durations times --dui-motion-scale and --dui-motion-enabled, distances times --dui-motion-movement.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-motion-duration-fast` | `calc(150ms * 1 * 1)` | `calc(150ms * 1 * 1)` | Small state changes: hover, press, switch, popovers and menus |
| `--dui-motion-duration-normal` | `calc(250ms * 1 * 1)` | `calc(250ms * 1 * 1)` | Dialogs and toasts |
| `--dui-motion-duration-slow` | `calc(350ms * 1 * 1)` | `calc(350ms * 1 * 1)` | Large surfaces that travel: the drawer |
| `--dui-motion-distance` | `calc(0.75rem * 1)` | `calc(0.75rem * 1)` | How far a dialog or toast lifts as it fades in; 0 with reduced motion |
| `--dui-motion-zoom` | `calc(1 - (1 - 0.95) * 1)` | `calc(1 - (1 - 0.95) * 1)` | Scale a popover or menu grows from; 1 (no zoom) with reduced motion |

### Elevation

A shadow and a surface per level. Every level from 1 up is a 1px ring in the hairline color (--dui-color-border) plus layers with a negative spread, so an elevated component needs no border of its own. Light scheme: the shadow does the work and every level keeps --dui-color-surface. Dark scheme: shadows barely show on a dark page, so each level also mixes --dui-elevation-surface-step more of the text color into its surface, and levels 2 to 4 add a 1px top inset highlight. The ring reads slightly brighter in dark, because the dark hairline is the light text color at low alpha.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-elevation-shadow-color` | `color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow color after strength; retune --dui-color-shadow and --dui-elevation-strength |
| `--dui-elevation-ring` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%)` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%)` | The 1px hairline ring included in every elevated role |
| `--dui-elevation-highlight` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%)` | Dark scheme only: a 1px top inset highlight on levels 2 to 4 |
| `--dui-elevation-0` | `none` | `none` | Level 0, flat: no shadow |
| `--dui-elevation-1` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Level 1: the ring and a 1px shadow |
| `--dui-elevation-2` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Level 2: ring, two layers, dark highlight |
| `--dui-elevation-3` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 4px 8px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 12px 24px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 4px 8px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 12px 24px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Level 3: ring, two layers, dark highlight |
| `--dui-elevation-4` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 8px 16px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 24px 48px -12px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 8px 16px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 24px 48px -12px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Level 4: ring, two layers, dark highlight |
| `--dui-elevation-0-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg)` | Level 0 surface: the page |
| `--dui-elevation-1-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) 3%, oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Level 1 surface: one step lighter in dark |
| `--dui-elevation-2-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 2), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Level 2 surface: two steps lighter in dark |
| `--dui-elevation-3-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 3), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Level 3 surface: three steps lighter in dark |
| `--dui-elevation-4-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 4), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Level 4 surface: four steps lighter in dark |

### Elevation by role

Components use these, never the numbers.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-elevation-flat` | `none` | `none` | Shadow of content on the page |
| `--dui-elevation-flat-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg)` | Surface of content on the page |
| `--dui-elevation-raised` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow of cards |
| `--dui-elevation-raised-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) 3%, oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Surface of cards |
| `--dui-elevation-panel` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow of floating panels: an app shell's sidebars, the docs sidebar and table of contents |
| `--dui-elevation-panel-surface` | `oklch(98.2% 0.003 265deg)` | `oklch(19% 0.007 265deg)` | Surface of floating panels: the raised surface, one step off the page |
| `--dui-elevation-overlay` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 2px 4px -2px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 4px 12px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow of toasts and other non-modal layers over the page |
| `--dui-elevation-overlay-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 2), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Surface of non-modal layers over the page |
| `--dui-elevation-popover` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 4px 8px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 12px 24px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 4px 8px -4px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 12px 24px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow of popovers, menus, tooltips and nav dropdowns |
| `--dui-elevation-popover-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 3), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Surface of popovers, menus and nav dropdowns |
| `--dui-elevation-dialog` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 transparent, 0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 8px 16px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent), 0 24px 48px -12px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 6%), 0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 8px 16px -8px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent), 0 24px 48px -12px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Shadow of dialogs and drawers |
| `--dui-elevation-dialog-surface` | `oklch(99.3% 0.002 265deg)` | `color-mix(in oklab, oklch(95% 0.004 265deg) calc(3% * 4), oklch(16.5% 0.006 265deg))` | Surface of dialogs and drawers |

### Density

Space inside components and control heights, from the comfortable value (--dui-density-scale 1) down to the compact one (0). Compact controls stay 32px tall, above the 24px of WCAG 2.5.8. Type sizes never change with density.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-size-control` | `calc(2rem + (2.75rem - 2rem) * 1)` | `calc(2rem + (2.75rem - 2rem) * 1)` | Min block size of controls, buttons and nav, menu and listbox items: 44px comfortable, 32px compact |
| `--dui-space-control-block` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | Block padding inside controls, buttons and items: 0.5rem comfortable, 0.25rem compact |
| `--dui-space-control-inline` | `calc(0.5rem + (0.75rem - 0.5rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.5rem + (0.75rem - 0.5rem) * 1)` | Inline padding of text fields and nav, menu and listbox items: 0.75rem comfortable, 0.5rem compact |
| `--dui-space-button-inline` | `calc(0.75rem + (1rem - 0.75rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.75rem + (1rem - 0.75rem) * 1)` | Inline padding of buttons: 1rem comfortable, 0.75rem compact |
| `--dui-space-gap` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | Gap between the parts of a control: icon and label, check and label: 0.5rem comfortable, 0.25rem compact |
| `--dui-space-gap-tight` | `calc(0.125rem + (0.25rem - 0.125rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.125rem + (0.25rem - 0.125rem) * 1)` | Gap and padding in groups of controls: field, toolbar, pagination, menu: 0.25rem comfortable, 0.125rem compact |
| `--dui-space-cell` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | `calc(0.25rem + (0.5rem - 0.25rem) * 1)` | Table cell padding: 0.5rem comfortable, 0.25rem compact |

See CHANGELOG.md.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-shadow-raised` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(21.5% 0.012 265deg / 11%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(25% 0.015 265deg / 12%) 100%, transparent)` | `0 0 0 1px oklch(95% 0.004 265deg / 10%), 0 1px 2px -1px color-mix(in srgb, oklch(14% 0.015 265deg / 46%) 100%, transparent)` | Deprecated: use --dui-elevation-raised (level 1) |
| `--dui-duration-fast` | `calc(150ms * 1 * 1)` | `calc(150ms * 1 * 1)` | Deprecated: use --dui-motion-duration-fast |
| `--dui-duration-normal` | `calc(250ms * 1 * 1)` | `calc(250ms * 1 * 1)` | Deprecated: use --dui-motion-duration-normal |
| `--dui-easing-standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Deprecated: use --dui-motion-easing-standard |

## Base elements

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.html

Native HTML elements styled by the base layer, with no classes.

### Live example

#### Text

```html
<h1>Heading level 1</h1>
<h2>Heading level 2</h2>
<h3>Heading level 3</h3>
<h4>Heading level 4</h4>
<h5>Heading level 5</h5>
<h6>Heading level 6</h6>
<p>
  A paragraph with a <a href="#text-title">link to this section</a>, some <strong>strong importance</strong>,
  <em>stress emphasis</em>, a <mark>highlighted run</mark>, an abbreviation like
  <abbr title="Web Content Accessibility Guidelines">WCAG</abbr>, inline <code>&lt;code&gt;</code>,
  sample output <samp>Saved.</samp>, and keyboard input <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>.
  Prose is capped at a comfortable measure so lines stay readable on wide screens.
</p>
<p><small>Small print: side comments such as legal text use <code>&lt;small&gt;</code>.</small></p>
<p>H<sub>2</sub>O and E = mc<sup>2</sup> keep their line height.</p>
<hr>
<blockquote cite="https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1">
  <p>If you can use a native HTML element or attribute with the semantics and behavior you require already built in, instead of re-purposing an element and adding an ARIA role, state or property to make it accessible, then do so.</p>
  <footer>From <cite><a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1">Using ARIA, first rule</a></cite></footer>
</blockquote>
```

#### Lists

```html
<div class="grid">
  <div>
    <h3>Unordered</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>Native elements first</li>
      <li>Tokens as custom properties
        <ul>
          <li>Primitive</li>
          <li>Semantic</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>Cascade layers</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h3>Ordered</h3>
    <ol>
      <li>Link the stylesheet</li>
      <li>Write semantic HTML</li>
      <li>Override tokens to theme</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h3>Description</h3>
    <dl>
      <dt>Primitive token</dt>
      <dd>A raw value, named by what it is.</dd>
      <dt>Semantic token</dt>
      <dd>A role, pointing at a primitive.</dd>
    </dl>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Preformatted code

```html
        <pre><code>&lt;link rel="stylesheet" href="css/domestic.css"&gt;

:root {
  --dui-color-accent: light-dark(#7a2e8c, #e2a8f0);
  --dui-font-heading: charter, "Bitstream Charter", "Sitka Text", cambria, serif;
}</code></pre>
        <pre data-scroll="inline" tabindex="0" aria-label="Copy the CSS into a project"><code>git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui.git &amp;&amp; cp -R domestic-ui/css public/css &amp;&amp; rm -rf domestic-ui</code></pre>
```

### Attributes

None: write semantic HTML.

- `data-color-scheme="light" | "dark"`

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [`css/base/document.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/document.css) | Document, color scheme, rhythm and focus. |
| [`css/base/forms.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/forms.css) | – |
| [`css/base/interactive.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/interactive.css) | – |
| [`css/base/media.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/media.css) | – |
| [`css/base/tables.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/tables.css) | – |
| [`css/base/typography.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/typography.css) | – |

### Accessibility

- Links keep their underline, so color is never the only cue ([WCAG 1.4.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- Every focusable element shows a `:focus-visible` outline in `--dui-color-focus`, the system `highlight` color in forced colors ([WCAG 2.4.7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html)).
- `scroll-padding-block` keeps focused elements clear of sticky edges ([WCAG 2.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html)).
- Text controls, buttons and summaries are at least `--dui-size-target` tall ([WCAG 2.5.8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).
- Checkboxes, radios and range keep native rendering, tinted with `accent-color`.
- Open a `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or `command="show-modal"` so the browser handles focus, <kbd>Esc</kbd> and inertness ([APG Dialog (Modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)).
- Duration tokens are `0s` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- CSS cannot add semantics: label every control, group with `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, give tables a `<caption>` and `th scope`, and images `alt` ([Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)).

## Visually hidden

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/utilities/visually-hidden.html

Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree.

_Diagram: Visually hidden text names an icon-only button, such as the close button of a panel, for screen readers without showing on screen._

### Live example

#### Visually hidden

```html
<button type="button"><span aria-hidden="true">×</span> <span class="visually-hidden">Close the panel</span></button>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `class="visually-hidden"` |  |

- The technique from [The A11Y Project](https://www.a11yproject.com/posts/how-to-hide-content/).
- The content shows again on focus, so it works for skip links.

### Accessibility

- Screen readers read the content; it stays off screen until it is focused.

### Specifications

- [The A11Y Project how to hide content](https://www.a11yproject.com/posts/how-to-hide-content/)

### See also

- [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/utilities/visually-hidden.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/utilities/visually-hidden.css), [`examples/base.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/base.html)

- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Action bar

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/action-bar.html

A long form whose Save and Cancel buttons stay in a sticky bar at the bottom of the window, with scroll margins so the bar never hides the focused field (WCAG 2.4.11).

_Diagram: The action bar is a sticky strip at the bottom of the window under a long form, holding its Save and Cancel buttons._

### Live example

#### Edit customer

```html
<form class="stack" aria-labelledby="edit-form-title">
  <h3 id="edit-form-title">Analytical Engines Ltd.</h3>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-company">Company name</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-company" name="company" value="Analytical Engines Ltd." autocomplete="organization">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-number">Customer number</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-number" name="number" value="C-118" readonly>
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-vat">VAT number</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-vat" name="vat" value="GB 123 4567 89" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-contact">Contact person</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-contact" name="contact" value="Ada Lovelace" autocomplete="name">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-email">Email</label>
      <input type="email" id="ab-email" name="email" value="ada@analytical-engines.example" autocomplete="email">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-phone">Phone</label>
      <input type="tel" id="ab-phone" name="phone" value="+44 20 7946 0018" autocomplete="tel">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-street">Street and number</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-street" name="street" value="12 St James's Square" autocomplete="address-line1">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-postcode">Postal code</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-postcode" name="postcode" value="SW1Y 4JH" autocomplete="postal-code">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-city">City</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-city" name="city" value="London" autocomplete="address-level2">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-country">Country</label>
      <select id="ab-country" name="country" autocomplete="country">
        <option value="DE">Germany</option>
        <option value="NL">Netherlands</option>
        <option value="GB" selected>United Kingdom</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-terms">Payment terms</label>
      <select id="ab-terms" name="terms">
        <option>14 days net</option>
        <option selected>30 days net</option>
        <option>60 days net</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-limit">Credit limit (€)</label>
      <input type="number" id="ab-limit" name="limit" value="5000" min="0" step="100">
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-notes">Internal notes</label>
      <textarea id="ab-notes" name="notes">Prefers delivery before noon.</textarea>
    </div>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="ab-reference">Purchase order reference</label>
      <input type="text" id="ab-reference" name="reference" value="PO-AE-2025-07" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
  <footer data-action-bar>
    <button type="submit">Save customer</button>
    <button type="reset">Cancel</button>
  </footer>
</form>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Where | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-action-bar` | a `<footer>` (or `<div>`) that is the last child of a `<form>` | holds that form's buttons |

The Save and Cancel buttons of a long form, kept in view: a bar at the end of the \<form> that sticks to the bottom of the scroll area while the form scrolls, and comes to rest after the last field when the end of the form is reached. Built with position: sticky, so it never leaves its form and needs no script. The buttons wrap onto a second row on narrow screens.

Our choice: the bar is the last child of the \<form> it submits, so its buttons submit and reset that form with no form="…" attribute, and the sticky bar stops at the form's end instead of covering what follows.

#### Elevation

`--dui-elevation-overlay` and its surface (level 2), whose 1px ring draws the edge so it reads as above the fields it covers; the transparent border is what forced colors mode paints.

#### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves from the last field to the bar's buttons; a focused field is scrolled clear of the bar |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | in a text field, submits the form (native) |

### Accessibility

- Buttons sit at the inline end in source order, never reversed with CSS, so the Tab order follows the visual order (WCAG 2.4.3); put the primary action (type="submit") first.
- A sticky bar must not hide the field that has focus (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)).
- Every ancestor of a form with an action bar gets a scroll-padding at its block end as tall as a bar with two rows of buttons, so when Tab moves to a field under the bar, the browser scrolls it clear above the bar (WCAG technique C43).
- Because it is set on every ancestor, it works in whichever one scrolls: the page or a pane that scrolls on its own.
- Buttons keep their target size (44px, 32px compact; WCAG 2.5.8).
- The bar is a \<footer> of the form, which is not a landmark inside a form.
- Give the bar no role; its buttons say what they do ("Save customer").
- The reserved space covers two rows of buttons: keep the bar to two or three short labels, so it never wraps to a third row at 320px; put further actions in a menu button.

### Specifications

- [MDN `sticky`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position#sticky)
- [MDN `scroll-padding`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-padding)
- [WCAG Focus not obscured minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html)
- [WCAG C43](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C43)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/layout/action-bar.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/action-bar.css), [`examples/layouts/action-bar.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/layouts/action-bar.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Cluster

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.html

An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).

_Diagram: A cluster is a row of buttons, tags or nav links under a heading that wraps onto a second line when the row is full._

### Live example

#### Cluster

```html
<ul class="cluster card">
  <li><code>reset</code></li>
  <li><code>tokens</code></li>
  <li><code>base</code></li>
  <li><code>layout</code></li>
  <li><code>components</code></li>
  <li><code>utilities</code></li>
</ul>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `class="cluster"` |  |
| `--cluster-gap` | space between items (default: `var(--dui-space-s)`) |
| `--cluster-justify` | justify-content value (default: flex-start) |
| `--cluster-align` | align-items value (default: center) |

Pattern: "The Cluster", Every Layout, built with flex-wrap and gap.

The custom properties do not inherit, so nested clusters keep their defaults.

### Specifications

- [Every Layout cluster](https://every-layout.dev/layouts/cluster/)

## Grid

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.html

A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.

_Diagram: A grid lays out cards or panels in the content area in as many equal columns as fit, here three columns and two rows._

### Live example

#### Grid

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 12rem">
  <article class="card">
    <h4>Atoms</h4>
    <p>Native elements styled by the base layer, plus a few attributes.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="card">
    <h4>Molecules</h4>
    <p>Small groups of atoms, such as tabs, dialogs and cards.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="card">
    <h4>Organisms</h4>
    <p>Larger sections built from molecules. Coming later.</p>
  </article>
</div>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `class="grid"` |  |
| `--grid-min` | minimum column width (default: `var(--dui-size-column-min)`) |
| `--grid-gap` | gap between cells (default: `var(--dui-space-l)`) |

No media queries. Pattern: "RAM" (repeat, auto-fit, minmax), see and "The Grid", Every Layout.

The custom properties do not inherit, so nested grids keep their defaults.

### Specifications

- [MDN `auto-fit`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat#auto-fit)
- [Every Layout grid](https://every-layout.dev/layouts/grid/)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)

- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/layout/grid.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/grid.css), [`examples/base.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/base.html)

## Scroll

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/scroll.html

A scroll container for content wider than the screen, such as a data table, so it scrolls on its own instead of widening the page.

_Diagram: A scroll region holds a data table wider than the content area, so the table scrolls sideways on its own and the page does not._

### Live example

#### Scroll region

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="viewports-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="viewports-caption">Viewports every page is checked at</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col">Width</th>
        <th scope="col">Height</th>
        <th scope="col">Engines</th>
        <th scope="col">Checks</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>320px</td>
        <td>640px</td>
        <td>Chromium, Firefox, WebKit</td>
        <td>No sideways page scroll, no axe violations</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>375px</td>
        <td>812px</td>
        <td>Chromium, Firefox, WebKit</td>
        <td>No sideways page scroll, no axe violations</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</section>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `data-scroll="inline"` | scroll along the inline axis (left/right in English) |
| `data-scroll="block inline"` | also scroll along the block axis, at most `--dui-size-pane` (the viewport) tall, so a sticky table header stays in view (`css/components/organisms/data-table.css`) |

- Add `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can scroll it ([WCAG 2.1.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html), [axe rule](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable)).
- **Our choice:** a `<section>` with `aria-labelledby`, not `<div role="region">`, because the native element already has the role.
- A table inside keeps `display: table`, or it can lose its semantics ([Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html)).

### Accessibility

- [WCAG 1.4.10](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html) allows two-dimensional scrolling for data tables.
- A named `<section>` is a region landmark ([HTML-AAM](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section)), so the focus stop is announced.

### Specifications

- [Deque University scrollable region focusable](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable)
- [W3C el section](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section)
- [Adrian Roselli tables css display properties and aria](https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html)
- [WCAG Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)
- [MDN `overflow-x`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-x)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/layout/scroll.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/scroll.css), [`examples/base.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/base.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Scroller](https://vercel.com/geist/scroller)

## Stack

Vertical flow with a consistent gap between children.

#### Stack

```html

  <p>Stack item one</p>
  <p>Stack item two, with <code>--stack-gap: var(--dui-space-xs)</code></p>

</div>
```

### API

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `class="stack"` |  |
| `--stack-gap` | space between children (default: `var(--dui-space-m)`) |

Pattern: "The Stack", Every Layout, built with flexbox gap.

--stack-gap does not inherit, so nested stacks keep their own default.

## Atoms

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.html

Small additions to the base layer, for what a native element cannot express on its own. A level of [Atomic Design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/); APIs follow the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Our choices

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

- **Our choice:** one `data-<atom>` attribute per atom, whose value is a space-separated list matched with [`~=`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors). One attribute is one API to learn, it reads as a sentence (`data-button="primary small"`), and it cannot pile up like modifier classes.
- **Our choice:** `data-button` with no variant word keeps the native default (a submit button is primary, everything else is secondary), so M1 markup keeps working and the attribute is only needed when the native type does not match the emphasis you want.
- **Our choice:** the quiet button uses the accent color for its text, so it still reads as interactive without a border. Use it next to other buttons, not inside running text, where a real link belongs.
- **Our choice:** primary buttons add an inner focus ring in their text color on top of the shared outline, so the indicator contrasts with the fill as well as the surface. This is the double-ring technique described in [WCAG technique C40](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C40).
- **Our choice:** small buttons are 32px tall: below the 44px default, above the [24px minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- **Our choice:** `aria-disabled="true"` looks exactly like `disabled`. Prefer native `disabled`; use `aria-disabled` when users should be able to reach the control and read why it is unavailable.
- **Our choice:** the field's error text starts with the word "Error:" in the markup, rather than a CSS icon, so every user and every screen reader gets it with no extra API. Invalid controls also get a thick start border, a shape change as well as a color change.
- **Our choice:** errors are tied to controls with `aria-describedby`, not `aria-errormessage`, because `aria-describedby` has broader screen reader support today (see the support notes on [MDN `aria-errormessage`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-errormessage)).
- **Our choice:** the switch is the native checkbox with `role="switch"`, drawn with `appearance: none` and one pseudo-element. The thumb moves and changes color, and forced-colors mode gets explicit system colors.
- **Our choice:** badge tones are 8% of the tone mixed into the surface, with the tone as text. The tinted surfaces are derived tokens (`--dui-color-*-surface`), so a theme that changes the surface or a tone re-tints badges with no extra overrides.
- **Our choice:** icons are [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) SVGs pasted inline, with no icon files, sprite, font or package in the repository, because Lucide already draws in our 24px, 2px, `currentColor` stroke and inline SVG needs no build and follows forced colors. The hook is `data-icon` on the `<svg>`, the same one-attribute rule as every atom, rather than `svg[aria-hidden]`, which would also style meaningful `role="img"` graphics and tie the look to an accessibility attribute. The rules for when to use an icon are in [PRINCIPLES.md](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/opinions-we-hold.md#icons).
- **Our choice:** an icon-only button (`data-button="icon"`) is named by visually hidden text inside it, not `aria-label`, because real text is translated by browser translation tools and copied with the page. Its `<dui-tooltip>` shows the same words and is `aria-hidden`, so the name is announced once; with JavaScript off the button keeps its name.
- **Our choice:** a field is an atom here, not a molecule, because a control is not usable without its label, hint and error. Larger compositions (forms, cards, headers) are molecules and organisms for later milestones.

### Not shipped, and why

| Candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Divider | Cut. `<hr>` is the native thematic break and is already styled in the base layer. A class would duplicate it. |
| Avatar | Cut. There is no standard or APG pattern for it; it is an `<img alt>` with a radius and a size, which the base layer and one line of your CSS already give. Revisit with a real use case (initials fallback, image loading). |
| Danger button variant | Not added. Not requested, and a destructive action is better marked by its label and a confirmation `<dialog>` than by color. Easy to add later as one more variant word. |
| Spinner for loading | Not added. The honest state is the changed label plus `aria-busy`; a spinner that replaces the label hides it from everyone. |

## Text helpers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/text.html

Lead, small and muted text helpers from domestic-ui, with copyable markup.

_Diagram: The lead paragraph sits right under a page's heading in larger text, and small muted text holds metadata such as a last-updated line at the end._

### Live example

#### Lead paragraph

```html
<p data-text="lead">Plan your week in five minutes. Everything else stays out of the way.</p>
<p>Regular body text follows at the normal size.</p>
```

#### Small and muted

```html
<p data-text="small">Prices include tax.</p>
<p data-text="muted">Shared with 3 people.</p>
<p data-text="small muted">Last updated <time datetime="2026-05-03">3 May 2026</time>.</p>
```

### Attributes

`data-text="lead | small | muted"` (combinable)

| Attribute or value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `data-text="lead \| small \| muted"` |  |

Values are a space-separated list, so they combine: `data-text="small muted"`.

- Values combine: `data-text="small muted"`.
- Size and color only. For meaning, use [`<small>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element), `<strong>` or `<em>`.

### Accessibility

- Muted text uses `--dui-color-text-muted`, tested at 4.5:1 on every surface ([WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)).

### Specifications

- [WHATWG text-level semantics](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html)
- [WCAG 1.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- [WHATWG the small element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element)

### See also

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md)
- [Component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api)
- [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
- Source: [`css/components/atoms/text.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/text.css), [`examples/atoms/text.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/text.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Typography](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography)
- [Material Design 3: Typography](https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/overview)
