```html
          <tr><td>Shipping</td><td>1</td><td>€80.00</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>
  </section>
  <aside aria-labelledby="payments-title">
    <h3 id="payments-title">Payments</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>14 March 2025: €500.00 by bank transfer</li>
      <li>28 March 2025: €400.00 by bank transfer</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Open: €340.00</strong></p>
    <p><a href="?invoice=INV-2025-0318&amp;view=reminder">Send a payment reminder</a></p>
  </aside>
</div>
```

#### Shipping and billing (1:1)

```html
<div data-split>
  <section aria-labelledby="ship-title">
    <h3 id="ship-title">Ship to</h3>
    <address>
      Analytical Engines Ltd.<br>
      12 St James's Square<br>
      London SW1Y 4JH<br>
      United Kingdom
    </address>
  </section>
  <section aria-labelledby="bill-title">
    <h3 id="bill-title">Bill to</h3>
    <address>
      Analytical Engines Ltd., Accounts payable<br>
      PO Box 1815<br>
      London EC1A 1BB<br>
      United Kingdom
    </address>
  </section>
</div>
```

#### Customer and activity (1:2)

```html
<div data-split="1:2">
  <section aria-labelledby="summary-title">
    <h3 id="summary-title">Bletchley Instruments</h3>
    <dl>
      <dt>Customer since</dt>
      <dd>2019</dd>
      <dt>Orders this year</dt>
      <dd>18</dd>
    </dl>
  </section>
  <section aria-labelledby="activity-title">
    <h3 id="activity-title">Recent activity</h3>
    <ol>
      <li>Order 1041 shipped by PostNL, 11 March 2025</li>
      <li>Invoice INV-2025-0301 paid in full, 4 March 2025</li>
      <li>Credit note CN-2025-0012 issued for a damaged reader, 27 February 2025</li>
    </ol>
  </section>
</div>
```

### Attributes

| Attribute or value | Where | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-split="[1:1 \| 1:2 \| 2:1]"` | the wrapper of exactly two regions | empty means 1:1 (equal halves) |

#### Breakpoint

40rem of the wrapper's own inline size. A container query condition cannot read a custom property, so it is written as a length; to move it, write your own @container dui-split rule.

### Accessibility

- The divider is not draggable: a resizable divider is the APG Window Splitter pattern (role="separator" with aria-valuenow and arrow keys) and needs script, so it is out of scope; see explainers/split-view.md.
- Source order is the reading and Tab order in both layouts; the ratio never reorders the regions (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
- Nothing scrolls sideways at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).

### Specifications

- [APG Window Splitter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/)
- [WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)
- [MDN Grid layout](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout)
- [MDN Container queries](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Containment/Container_queries)

### See also

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md)
- Source: [`css/layout/split.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/split.css), [`examples/layouts/split.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/layouts/split.html)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views)
- [Material Design 3: Scaffold: Panes](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/panes)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Web components

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/web-components.html

Each element's attributes, keyboard and accessibility are on the page of the pattern it enhances.

A few small [custom elements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_custom_elements),
each added only because native HTML cannot do the job. Before reaching for one, check whether an
element already covers it: `<dialog>`, `<details>`, the
[`popover`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/popover)
attribute and [invoker commands](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API)
handle many cases that used to need script, and most molecules need none.

### The rule

Every element here:

- exists because HTML or CSS cannot do something, and its header comment says what;
- enhances native markup that already works without JavaScript
  ([progressive enhancement](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Progressive_Enhancement)):
  content stays readable and links, buttons and sections stay usable with the script off;
- uses the **light DOM**: no shadow root, so the [molecule CSS](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md)
  and your own CSS style the markup directly, and there is no second styling API;
- follows the matching [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) pattern,
  and adds ARIA roles only when it also adds the keyboard behavior those roles promise;
- is one ES module with no dependencies and no build step, named with the `dui-` prefix, and
  documents its API, events and keyboard in its header comment.

Load one from a page with a module script; it upgrades matching elements already in the page and
any added later:

```html
<script type="module" src="web-components/dui-tabs.js"></script>
```

### Index

#### `<dui-tabs>`

No tabs element: one panel at a time, roving tabindex and arrow keys ([APG Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/)). Upgrades a `<nav>` of in-page links and `<section>` panels; `aria-current="true"` on a link selects it on load.

Styles: [tabs.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md). Example: [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md). Source: [`dui-tabs.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-tabs.js).

#### `<dui-menu>`

`popovertarget` opens the list, but there is no menu widget: arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, opening on a chosen item ([APG Menu Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)).

Styles: [menu-button.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md). Example: [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md). Source: [`dui-menu.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-menu.js).

#### `<dui-combobox>`

`<input list>` suggests values, but the browser draws the popup: it cannot be styled, filters differently per engine and announces no result count. Builds an APG list autocomplete listbox from the `<datalist>` and keeps the same input ([APG Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)). See [Combobox (typeahead) explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/combobox.md).

Styles: [combobox.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md). Example: [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md). Source: [`dui-combobox.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-combobox.js).

#### `<dui-toolbar>`

No roving focus in HTML: one Tab stop with arrow keys between controls ([APG Toolbar](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/)).

Styles: [toolbar.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md). Example: [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md). Source: [`dui-toolbar.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-toolbar.js).

#### `<dui-tooltip>`

A popover cannot open on hover or focus yet. [`interestfor`](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/) is the coming standard (Chromium only today); this element stands in until it is interoperable.

Styles: [popover.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md). Example: [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md). Source: [`dui-tooltip.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-tooltip.js).

#### `<dui-toaster>`

A live region announces messages, but nothing builds a toast, adds its Dismiss button and moves focus sensibly when one goes away. See [Toast explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/toast.md).

Styles: [alerts.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md). Example: [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md). Source: [`dui-toaster.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-toaster.js).

#### `<dui-app-shell>`

A button cannot hide another element and keep `aria-expanded` in step, and a sidebar that is part of the page when wide must become a modal drawer only when the shell is narrow. Toggles `hidden` on a sidebar beside main, moves the one copy of a sidebar into a `<dialog data-dialog="drawer">` (`showModal()`) while it is open on a narrow shell, and switches mode on the shell's own width ([`ResizeObserver`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ResizeObserver)); toggles are `hidden` until it upgrades. See [App shell explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md).

Styles: [app-shell.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) (layout). Example: [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md). Source: [`dui-app-shell.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-app-shell.js).

#### `<dui-table>`

A table cannot reorder its rows, and a checkbox cannot check its siblings, count them or be indeterminate from markup. Adds sortable column buttons with `aria-sort` ([APG Sortable Table](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/examples/sortable-table/)), a "select all" checkbox, the selection count and bulk-action enabling to a native `<table>`; without it the table is a plain table with ordinary checkboxes.

Styles: [data-table.css](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md). Example: [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md). Source: [`dui-table.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-table.js).

### Events

| Element | Event | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<dui-tabs>` | `dui-tabs-change` | After the selected tab changes; `event.detail` is `{ tab, panel }`. Bubbles. |
| `<dui-combobox>` | `dui-combobox-filter` | On every input, before filtering; `event.detail` is `{ query }`. Bubbles; cancelable: cancel it to load options yourself, then call `setOptions()`. |
| `<dui-combobox>` | `change` (on the input) | When an option is accepted with Enter or a click, as a native control would. |
| `<dui-toaster>` | `dui-toast-dismiss` | Before a toast is removed. Bubbles; cancelable. |
| `<dui-app-shell>` | `dui-app-shell-toggle` | After a sidebar is expanded, collapsed, opened or closed; `event.detail` is `{ sidebar, edge, expanded, drawer }`. Bubbles. |
| `<dui-table>` | `dui-table-sort` | Before the rows move; `event.detail` is `{ column, index, direction }` (the `<th>`, its column index, `"ascending"` or `"descending"`). Bubbles; cancelable: cancel it to sort on the server, then set `aria-sort` and replace the rows yourself. |

`<dui-menu>`, `<dui-toolbar>` and `<dui-tooltip>` fire no events of their own (nor does `<dui-table>` for selection: listen for `change` on its checkboxes): listen for the native
`click` on items and controls, and the native `toggle` on popovers.

## Explainers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/index.html

An explainer describes a pattern that has **no native HTML element and no
[APG pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/)**, written the way a platform feature
would be proposed. The format follows the [W3C TAG explainer guidance](https://tag.w3.org/explainers/)
and the explainers published by [Open UI](https://open-ui.org/). Nothing here is a standard; each
file says which parts are **Our choice** and why.

### When an explainer is required

domestic-ui uses, in order: a native element, then the matching APG pattern, then ARIA only where
native HTML cannot express something ([PRINCIPLES.md](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/index.md)). A molecule that ends up
with neither a native element nor an APG pattern MUST have an explainer here, linked from the
header comment of its CSS file and from the
[molecules index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md). Layouts with no standard of their own (the [split view](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/split-view.md), the [app shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md)) may have one too.
Patterns that are backed by a standard
(dialog, details, popover, tabs, menu button, toolbar, breadcrumb, search) link to that standard
instead.

### Keywords

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Sections

Every explainer has these sections, in this order:

1. **Problem**: what authors cannot do well today.
2. **Use cases**: concrete situations.
3. **Goals** and 4. **Non-goals**.
5. **Proposed markup and API**: the attribute, element or methods we ship, with an example.
6. **Keyboard interaction**.
7. **Accessibility mappings**: roles, states, and what assistive technology users should hear.
8. **Alternatives considered**, each with why it was rejected.
9. **Prior art**, with links. We cite; we do not copy.
10. **Open questions**.

Names follow HTML and ARIA conventions (lowercase, no abbreviations, states in native attributes)
so a pattern could map onto a future native element or attribute.

### Index

| Explainer | Summary | CSS | Example | Script |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/card.md) | A self-contained summary with a heading, optional media and actions; a whole-card link whose name is the heading | [`card.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md) | [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md) | None |
| [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/pagination.md) | Links between pages of a list in a named `<nav>`, with `aria-current="page"` and non-link disabled ends | [`pagination.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md) | [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md) | None |
| [Drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/drawer.md) | A `<dialog>` variant at the inline-start or inline-end edge, full block size | [`dialog.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md) | [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md) | None |
| [Toast](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/toast.md) | A fixed `role="status"` region that stacks short messages that never dismiss themselves | [`alerts.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md) | [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md) | [`dui-toaster.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-toaster.js) |
| [Combobox](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/combobox.md) | How domestic-ui maps the APG list autocomplete combobox onto `<input list>` and `<datalist>`, and the choices the APG leaves open | [`combobox.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md) | [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md) | [`dui-combobox.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-combobox.js) |
| [Density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/density.md) | `data-density="compact"` on any element: tighter control heights, padding and table cells, same text size, targets at least 24px | [`semantic.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md) | [Compact density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.md) | None |
| [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md) | `data-app-shell`: app bar, primary sidebar, main and an auxiliary sidebar as native landmarks in named grid areas; one copy of each sidebar, collapsible beside main and a modal drawer when the shell is narrow; why not a dialog, popover, `<details>`, checkbox hack or duplicated navigation | [`app-shell.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) | [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) | [`dui-app-shell.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-app-shell.js) |
| [Auxiliary sidebar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/aux-sidebar.md) | The `<aside>` after `<main>` in an app shell: context for the selection, beside main from 64rem, a drawer at the end below; stable name, polite status on change | [`app-shell.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) | [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) | [`dui-app-shell.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-app-shell.js) |
| [Split view](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/split-view.md) | Two regions side by side at a fixed ratio (`data-split`) or a list of links beside a detail pane (`data-list-detail`), switched by a container query; why there is no draggable divider | [`split.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md), [`list-detail.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md) | [Split](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md) | None |
| [Code highlighting](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/code-highlighting.md) | `::highlight(dui-code-*)` names a page registers with the CSS Custom Highlight API, each colored by a `--dui-color-code-*` token at 4.5:1 on the code background | [`typography.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md) | [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md) | None (the page registers ranges) |

## App shell

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as a layout (`data-app-shell`) plus one web component (`<dui-app-shell>`).
CSS: [`css/layout/app-shell.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) ·
Script: [`web-components/dui-app-shell.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-app-shell.js) ·
Examples: [`examples/app-shell.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) (a full orders screen),
[`examples/layouts/app-shell.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) (a contained shell)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Business applications share one frame: an app bar across the top, navigation down one side, the work in
the middle, and often a second sidebar with the context of what is selected. HTML has the landmarks for
every part (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`) and the
[APG Landmark Regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/) practice says how to
label them, but no standard says how they become an app frame that collapses its sidebars and turns them
into drawers on a phone. Common implementations:

- render the navigation twice (a sidebar and a mobile menu), so screen reader users meet two
  navigation landmarks and the markup drifts apart;
- keep the sidebar in a `role="dialog"` at every width, so the permanent sidebar of a desktop page is
  announced as a dialog;
- switch on the viewport width, so a shell inside a docs page or a resizable panel picks the wrong mode;
- hide the sidebar with a CSS checkbox hack or `transform`, leaving it in the Tab order or with no
  `aria-expanded` on its button;
- show a "Menu" button that does nothing before (or without) JavaScript.

### Use cases

- An operations screen: orders in a table, the main navigation on the left, the selected order on the right.
- A settings area: navigation groups beside a long form.
- The same application on a phone: navigation and details open as drawers from their edges.
- A shell embedded in a page section (a documentation example, a preview pane), sized by its box.

### Goals

- Native landmarks in source order, which is also the reading and Tab order at every width
  ([2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html)).
- One copy of each sidebar in the DOM, in every mode.
- Everything visible and usable with JavaScript off: no dead buttons, the current page marked.
- Wide: each sidebar collapses and expands with a disclosure button; main takes the space.
- Narrow: each sidebar opens as a modal drawer with everything a modal dialog does.
- The mode follows the shell's own width, so a contained shell works anywhere.
- Layouts and organisms inside main respond to the width main actually has.
- No horizontal scrolling at 320px ([1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html));
  motion from the tokens, off under reduced motion
  ([2.3.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html)).

### Non-goals

- Resizable sidebars (see [Open questions](#open-questions)).
- A sidebar shrunk to a rail of icons. A rail needs tooltips or visible names for every icon and a second
  layout of the same links; collapsing to hidden is simpler and fully accessible.
- Persisting the collapsed state across visits (an event makes it possible; storage is the page's job).
- Routing: links in the navigation load pages; a single-page app may intercept them.

### Proposed markup and API

- The shell MUST be one element with `data-app-shell`: `<dui-app-shell data-app-shell>` to get the
  toggles' behavior, or any wrapper element for a static shell.
- A skip link to `<main>` MUST come before the shell, as its own first focusable element
  ([2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks.html)).
- Its children, in this order: a `<header>` (the app bar); the primary sidebar; `<main>`; an optional
  auxiliary `<aside>`; an optional `<footer>`. Parts are recognized by element and position, so they need
  no attributes: the `<nav>` or `<aside>` before `<main>` is the primary sidebar, the `<aside>` after it the
  auxiliary one.
- The primary sidebar SHOULD be a `<nav aria-label>` (usually with `data-nav="vertical"`). It MAY be an
  `<aside aria-label>` holding the primary `<nav>` when it also holds things that are not links (a
  workspace switcher). It MUST NOT be a `<div>`: it would not be a landmark.
- Every `<nav>` and `<aside>` MUST have an accessible name that does not repeat its role ("Main",
  "Order details"); two landmarks of the same kind MUST have different names.
- A sidebar with a toggle MUST have an `id`. Its toggle is a `<button type="button" aria-controls="id"
  aria-expanded="true" hidden>`; it MUST carry `hidden` in the markup, so it never shows without the
  script. `aria-expanded="false"` in the markup starts the sidebar collapsed when it sits beside main (an
  aux sidebar on a busy screen). At least one toggle MUST be outside the sidebar.
- `data-app-shell="contained"` makes the shell `--dui-size-pane` tall with its own scroll area; set
  `--dui-size-pane` on it to size it.
- Tokens: `--dui-size-sidebar` (16rem) and `--dui-size-sidebar-aux` (20rem) are the sidebar widths beside
  main; `--dui-size-pane` bounds a sidebar's height beside main.

```html
<a class="visually-hidden" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<dui-app-shell data-app-shell>
  <header>
    <button type="button" aria-controls="app-nav" aria-expanded="true" hidden>Menu</button>
    <a href="/">Northwind Operations</a>
    <button type="button" aria-controls="app-aux" aria-expanded="true" hidden>Details</button>
  </header>
  <nav id="app-nav" aria-label="Main" data-nav="vertical">…</nav>
  <main id="main">…</main>
  <aside id="app-aux" aria-label="Order details">…</aside>
</dui-app-shell>
<script type="module" src="web-components/dui-app-shell.js"></script>
```

#### Modes

| Shell width | Primary sidebar | Auxiliary sidebar | Without JavaScript |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| under 48rem | drawer at the start | drawer at the end | both stacked, above and below main |
| 48rem to 64rem | beside main, collapsible | drawer at the end | aux stacked under main |
| 64rem and up | beside main, collapsible | beside main, collapsible | both beside main |

The breakpoints are lengths in `@container dui-app-shell` rules (a container query cannot read a custom
property), and the same two numbers are in the script.

- In a drawer the sidebar element is moved into a `<dialog data-dialog="drawer start | end" closedby="any">`
  ([drawer explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/drawer.md)) that the element builds once, with a heading (the toggle's text) and a
  Close button, opened with [`showModal()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal).
  When it closes, the sidebar is moved back to where it was.
- `<main>` and each sidebar are named size containers (`dui-app-shell-main`, `dui-app-shell-start`,
  `dui-app-shell-end`); every layout and organism in domestic-ui switches on its own box, so they adapt to
  main's width. A page MAY write its own `@container dui-app-shell-main` rules.
- Methods `show(edge)`, `hide(edge)`, `toggle(edge)` and `isDrawer(edge)` (`"start"` or `"end"`) let a page
  open the details when a record is chosen. A `dui-app-shell-toggle` event reports every change.

**Our choice:** one copy of each sidebar, a plain landmark in its grid area, moved into a drawer only while
the drawer is open, so screen readers never hear "dialog" around a sidebar that is part of the page.

**Our choice:** the mode follows the shell's width (a `ResizeObserver` and container queries), not the
viewport, so a contained shell behaves like a full-window one.

### Keyboard interaction

- Tab / Shift+Tab: the skip link, the app bar, the primary sidebar, main, the auxiliary sidebar, the
  footer, in source order. A collapsed sidebar is `hidden`, so it is skipped.
- Enter / Space on a toggle (native button): collapses or expands its sidebar; on a narrow shell, opens it
  as a drawer and moves focus to the drawer's first focusable element (its Close button).
- Esc in a drawer: closes it; focus returns to the element that opened it (the toggle, or a link that
  called `show()`), and the toggle's `aria-expanded` becomes `false`.
- A click on the backdrop closes a drawer (`closedby="any"`, with a script fallback where it is not supported).
- Enter / Space on a group summary in the navigation: opens or closes the group (native `<details>`).

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name / state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<header>` (not inside a sectioning element) | `banner` ([HTML-AAM](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-header)) | |
| `<nav aria-label="Main">` | `navigation` | "Main" |
| `<main>` | `main` | |
| `<aside aria-label="Order details">` | `complementary` ([HTML-AAM](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-aside)) | "Order details" |
| `<footer>` | `contentinfo` | |
| Toggle | `button` | its text; [`aria-expanded`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-expanded) true while shown or open; [`aria-controls`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-controls) the sidebar |
| Collapsed sidebar | none ([`hidden`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/hidden)) | removed from the accessibility tree and the Tab order |
| Drawer | `dialog`, modal | its heading (the toggle's text); the rest of the page is inert |

What a screen reader user hears, for example: on a wide screen, "Menu, button, expanded", and in the
landmarks list "banner, Main navigation, main, Order details complementary, content information". On a
phone, "Menu, button, collapsed"; after Enter, "Menu, dialog, Close, button", then the "Main" navigation
inside it; after Esc, focus is back on "Menu, button, collapsed".

### Alternatives considered

- **(a) The sidebar always lives in a `<dialog>`**, opened with `show()` (non-modal, placed in the grid)
  when wide and `showModal()` when narrow. One copy, no DOM moves. Rejected: the permanent sidebar of a
  desktop page is announced as a dialog, a non-modal `<dialog>` is not a landmark, and with JavaScript off
  a closed dialog hides the navigation (an `open` attribute in the markup works around that but is
  discouraged by HTML).
- **(b) The sidebar is a plain landmark, moved into a drawer `<dialog>` while narrow.** Chosen, with one
  refinement: it is moved only while the drawer is open, not for the whole narrow mode, so between opens it
  sits hidden in its own place and a mode change never moves it.
- **(c) A [`popover`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/popover) instead
  of a dialog for the narrow mode.** A popover can be the sidebar itself (no move) and light-dismisses, but
  it is not modal: the page behind stays in the Tab order and the accessibility tree, which a full-height
  navigation drawer covering the page should not allow. Rejected for the drawer; it remains a candidate for
  a non-modal side panel (see the drawer explainer).
- **[`<details>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details) for
  collapse.** Works without script, but the summary must sit inside the sidebar, so the toggle cannot live
  in the app bar; the content cannot be a drawer; and a closed `<details>` cannot be shown again at a wider
  width without script. Rejected.
- **CSS-only checkbox hacks** (`:checked ~ nav`). The checkbox is announced as a checkbox, not a button with
  an expanded state, it stays in the Tab order with nothing to toggle when CSS lays everything out, and the
  drawer has no modality or Esc. Rejected.
- **Duplicated navigation** (a sidebar and a separate mobile menu). Two navigation landmarks with the same
  links, two places to mark the current page, and twice the markup for server rendering. Rejected.
- **Viewport media queries for the mode.** Break a shell inside a page section or a resizable pane.
  Rejected in favor of container queries and a `ResizeObserver` on the shell.

### Prior art

- [APG Landmark Regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/) and the
  [APG Disclosure pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/) (the toggles).
- [APG Dialog (Modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/) and the WHATWG
  [`<main>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-main-element) and
  [`<aside>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-aside-element) elements.
- MDN [`grid-template-areas`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/grid-template-areas),
  [container queries](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Containment/Container_queries) and
  [`ResizeObserver`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ResizeObserver).
- Design systems: Apple HIG [Sidebars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sidebars),
  Carbon [UI shell header](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/UI-shell-header/usage/),
  Primer [PageLayout](https://primer.style/components/page-layout),
  Atlassian [Page layout](https://atlassian.design/components/page-layout),
  GOV.UK [Service navigation](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/service-navigation/).
- [Open UI](https://open-ui.org/) has no app shell or sidebar proposal; this explainer is written so the
  parts could map onto native landmarks unchanged.

### Open questions

- **Resizable sidebars.** A draggable edge would follow the
  [APG Window Splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) pattern (a focusable
  `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow` and arrow keys), as noted for the [split view](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/split-view.md). Not
  built until a real use needs it.
- **Persisting the collapsed state.** The `dui-app-shell-toggle` event carries `expanded`; a page MAY store
  it (a cookie the server reads, so the markup can start with `aria-expanded="false"`, avoids a flash;
  [`localStorage`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage) works too).
  Should the element do this itself?
- **A flash on narrow screens.** With JavaScript on, the stacked sidebars show until the module runs. A
  server that knows the client is narrow can render the sidebars `hidden` and the toggles visible; should
  the element offer a hook for that?
- **Rails.** Is there a version of an icon rail that keeps names visible and needs no duplicate links?

## Auxiliary sidebar

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/aux-sidebar.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as part of the [app shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md): the `<aside>` after `<main>` in a
`data-app-shell`.
CSS: [`css/layout/app-shell.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) ·
Script: [`web-components/dui-app-shell.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-app-shell.js) ·
Example: [`examples/app-shell.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Work screens often show the context of what is selected next to the list it came from: the order chosen in
a table, the filters for a report, the activity on a record. HTML's
[`<aside>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-aside-element) is the element for
content related to the main content, but there is no standard for an aside that sits at the inline end of a
screen when there is room, gets out of the way when there is not, and can be dismissed. Common
implementations open a second, non-modal overlay that covers the table with no way to reach it by keyboard,
or rebuild the panel as a modal on phones with a second copy of its content.

### Use cases

- Details of the selected order beside the orders table (the
  [orders example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md)).
- Filters for a long report, kept open while scrolling it.
- An activity feed or comments on the record in main.

### Goals

- A complementary landmark with a name, after `<main>` in source order, so it is read and tabbed after
  the content it describes.
- Beside main when the shell is wide, stacked under main or a drawer at the end when it is not.
- Collapsible with a disclosure button, like the primary sidebar, and optionally collapsed from the start.
- Updated in place when the selection changes, with the change announced politely.
- Visible and usable with JavaScript off.

### Non-goals

- A non-modal overlay floating over main.
- More than one auxiliary sidebar.
- Tabs inside it: use [tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md) in the aside when it needs them.

### Proposed markup and API

- It MUST be an `<aside>` that is a child of the shell, after `<main>`, with an `id` and an accessible name
  (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) that stays the same when its content changes ("Order details", not
  "Order 1042").
- Its toggle is a `<button type="button" aria-controls="id" aria-expanded="true" hidden>` in the app bar
  (see the [app shell explainer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/app-shell.md)); `aria-expanded="false"` in the markup starts it collapsed.
- It sits beside main from 64rem of the shell's width (`--dui-size-sidebar-aux` wide, 20rem by default).
  Between 48rem and 64rem it is stacked under main without JavaScript and a drawer at the end with it, so
  on mid widths it starts collapsed; below 48rem it is a drawer at the end. **Our choice:** 64rem, because
  below that main would be narrower than a data table needs once both sidebars take their space.
- When a page changes its content (a row selected), it SHOULD say so in a polite
  [`role="status"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/status_role)
  element inside it, present from load, and it SHOULD NOT move focus. When the user explicitly asks to see a
  record (activates its link) and the aside is a drawer, the page MAY call `shell.show("end")`; focus moves
  into the drawer and returns to the link on Esc.
- Without JavaScript every record link SHOULD load a URL that renders the aside for that record (`?order=1042`).

```html
<aside id="app-aux" aria-label="Order details">
  <h2>Order 1042</h2>
  <dl>…</dl>
  <p role="status" class="visually-hidden"></p>
</aside>
```

**Our choice:** the aside's name is stable and its heading carries the record, so the landmarks list does not
change under the user, while heading navigation finds the record.

### Keyboard interaction

- Tab: reaches the aside after main (source order), when it is shown.
- Enter / Space on its toggle: collapses or expands it; when narrow, opens it as a drawer at the end.
- Esc in the drawer: closes it and returns focus to the element that opened it.

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name / state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<aside aria-label="Order details">` | `complementary` ([HTML-AAM](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-aside)) | "Order details" |
| Toggle | `button` | "Details"; `aria-expanded`; `aria-controls` the aside |
| Status inside | `status` (polite) | "Order 1040 shown in Order details." after a change |
| Drawer (narrow) | `dialog`, modal | the toggle's text |

A screen reader user selecting a row hears the checkbox state, then "Order 1040 shown in Order details."
without losing their place in the table.

### Alternatives considered

- **A popover at the inline end.** Non-modal and light-dismissed, so it covers the table while the table is
  still in the Tab order behind it. Rejected.
- **The details inside main, under the table** (a list-detail). Good when the details are the point of the
  screen; use [`data-list-detail`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md) then. The aside is for context that the
  user may hide.
- **A second copy of the details for phones.** Rejected for the same reason as a duplicated navigation: one
  copy, moved into the drawer while it is open.
- **Announcing every update with `aria-live` on the whole aside.** Rereads the whole panel on each change.
  Rejected for one short status message.

### Prior art

- [APG Landmark Regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/) (complementary).
- [WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html).
- Atlassian [Page layout](https://atlassian.design/components/page-layout) (right sidebar) and Primer
  [PageLayout](https://primer.style/components/page-layout) (pane).

### Open questions

- Should the aside remember its own collapsed state separately from the primary sidebar? The
  `dui-app-shell-toggle` event reports each edge separately, so a page can.
- Should a selection on a narrow screen open the drawer automatically? Today only an explicit link
  activation does, because opening a modal on every checkbox would be disruptive.

## Card

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/card.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as a styling contract.
CSS: [`css/components/molecules/card.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md) ·
Example: [`examples/molecules/card.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Cards are everywhere: lists of articles, products, projects. HTML has no card element and the
APG has no card pattern. Authors often make the whole card clickable by wrapping it in one big
`<a>` or by adding a click handler to a `<div>`. The first gives the link a very long accessible
name made of every word in the card. The second is invisible to keyboard and assistive
technology users. Secondary actions inside the card then become nested interactive content,
which HTML does not allow.

### Use cases

- A grid of articles where each card links to the article.
- A pricing grid where each card has a heading, details and one button.
- A project card that opens the project, with an "Edit" action next to it.

### Goals

- A card is ordinary sectioning content with a heading, so users can navigate by heading.
- A whole-card link keeps the heading as its accessible name.
- Secondary actions stay reachable with the pointer and the keyboard.
- Keyboard focus on the card link is clearly visible on the whole card.
- No JavaScript.

### Non-goals

- Layout of the card grid (use `.grid` from the layout layer).
- Selectable cards (checkbox cards) and draggable cards.
- Image loading, aspect ratios beyond `object-fit: cover`.

### Proposed markup and API

- A card MUST be an `<article>` when it makes sense on its own, else a `<section>` or `<li>`.
- A card MUST contain a heading (`h2`–`h6`).
- `data-card` on the element makes it a card. `data-card="link"` makes the whole card follow
  the first link inside its heading.
- Optional media is the first child: `<img>`, `<picture>` or `<video>`. Media SHOULD have
  `alt=""` when it only decorates.
- Actions go in a `<footer>` child. In a link card, every interactive element other than the
  heading link MUST be inside that `<footer>`.

```html
<article data-card="link">
  <img src="cover.jpg" alt="" width="640" height="360">
  <h3><a href="/guides/theming/">Theming guide</a></h3>
  <p>Override semantic tokens to make a theme.</p>
  <footer>
    <a href="/guides/theming/edit">Edit</a>
  </footer>
</article>
```

How it works: the heading link gets an `::after` pseudo-element with `position: absolute;
inset: 0`, so its hit area covers the card (the card is `position: relative`). The footer is
positioned above it with `z-index: 1`. The link's focus outline moves to the pseudo-element.

**Our choice:** the link lives in the heading, because the heading is the shortest text that
names the destination (WCAG 2.4.4).

### Keyboard interaction

- Tab: moves to the heading link, then to each footer action, in DOM order.
- Enter: follows the focused link.

A link card is one Tab stop plus its footer actions; body text is not focusable.

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<article data-card>` | `article` | none (not needed) |
| Heading | `heading` with its level | its text |
| Heading `<a href>` | `link` | the heading text only |
| Footer actions | `link` or `button` | their own text |

A screen reader user hears, for example, "heading level 3, link, Theming guide". Moving by
heading or by link reaches each card once. The media is skipped when `alt=""`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Wrap the whole card in `<a>`.** Rejected: the accessible name becomes every word in the
  card, and any button or link inside is nested interactive content, which the
  [HTML content model for `a`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)
  forbids.
- **A click handler on the card.** Rejected as the default: it needs JavaScript, and users of
  middle-click, "open in new tab" and link previews lose them. It does allow text selection;
  see the open questions.
- **`role="link"` on the card element.** Rejected: ARIA cannot give a `<div>` real link
  behavior, and it breaks the first rule of ARIA use
  ([Using ARIA](https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1)).

### Prior art

- Heydon Pickering, [Inclusive Components: Cards](https://inclusive-components.design/cards/),
  which describes both the pseudo-element overlay and the "redundant click event".
- [WHATWG `article` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element).
- [WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html)
  and [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html).
- [W3C images tutorial: decorative images](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/decorative/).

### Mapping to a future standard

`data-card="link"` describes "this region activates its primary link". If HTML gains a way to
declare a block-level click target that delegates to a link (an idea discussed in Open UI and
elsewhere), the attribute would map onto it and the pseudo-element would go away.

### Open questions

- Text in a link card cannot be selected with the mouse, because the overlay sits on top.
  Should a variant use the redundant click event (script) instead to allow selection?
- Should the card expose a hover style for touch users, who have no hover?
- Should cards in a list be `<li>` with `data-card`, so the list count is announced?

## Code highlighting

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/code-highlighting.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as CSS only. The page registers the ranges.
CSS: [`css/base/typography.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md) ·
Tokens: [`css/tokens/semantic.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md) ·
Example: [`examples/base.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Code samples read faster when keywords, strings and tags stand out. Most highlighters wrap every
token in a `<span class="...">`, which multiplies the DOM, ties the markup to one library's class
names, and puts colors in a theme file that ignores the system's tokens and dark scheme. HTML has
no element or attribute for a token's kind.

### Use cases

- Documentation pages that show HTML, CSS and JavaScript snippets.
- A product's own help or settings page that shows a config file.

### Goals

- No change to the markup: a `<pre><code>` stays plain text in the DOM.
- Colors come from semantic tokens, follow the color scheme and can be themed.
- Every color meets 4.5:1 on the code background in light and dark (WCAG 1.4.3).
- Without JavaScript the code is plain text, which is fine.
- No build step for users.

### Non-goals

- A tokenizer. Which ranges get which name is up to the page; the domestic-ui docs site registers
  them from `site/assets/highlight.js`.
- Languages other than HTML, CSS and JavaScript, line numbers, and diff markers.
- Bold or italic tokens: `::highlight()` cannot set `font-weight` or `font-style`.

### Proposed markup and API

The system ships one `::highlight()` rule per name, each setting `color` from a token. The page
creates [`Highlight`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Highlight) objects from
`Range`s over the text in `<code>` and registers them in `CSS.highlights` under these names:

| Highlight name | Covers | Token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dui-code-keyword` | JS keywords (`const`, `return`, `import`), CSS at-rules (`@layer`, `@media`) | `--dui-color-code-keyword` |
| `dui-code-string` | Quoted strings in JS and CSS, HTML attribute values | `--dui-color-code-string` |
| `dui-code-comment` | `<!-- -->`, `/* */` and `//` comments | `--dui-color-code-comment` |
| `dui-code-tag` | HTML tag names, CSS selectors | `--dui-color-code-tag` |
| `dui-code-attribute` | HTML attribute names | `--dui-color-code-attribute` |
| `dui-code-property` | CSS properties and custom properties, JS object properties | `--dui-color-code-property` |
| `dui-code-number` | Numbers with their units (`0.5rem`, `100%`, `42`) | `--dui-color-code-number` |
| `dui-code-punctuation` | `<`, `>`, `</`, `/>`, `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `:`, `;`, `,`, `=` | `--dui-color-code-punctuation` |

Anything not covered (CSS keyword values, identifiers, text content) stays `--dui-color-text`.
A range SHOULD NOT belong to two names; if it does, the later-registered highlight wins
([priority](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-highlight-api-1/#priorities)).

```js
const keywords = new Highlight(...rangesFor("keyword"));
CSS.highlights.set("dui-code-keyword", keywords);
```

**Our choice:** no `dui-code-value` name. HTML attribute values are strings, and coloring every
CSS keyword value made declarations harder to scan, not easier.

### Keyboard interaction

None. Highlights do not change focus, selection or the text.

### Accessibility mappings

- Highlights are not in the accessibility tree; screen readers read the plain text, as with no
  highlighting at all.
- Color is the only difference between tokens, and nothing depends on it (WCAG 1.4.1).
- In forced-colors mode every highlight is `CanvasText`.
- Text selection (`::selection`) still paints over highlights.

### Alternatives considered

- **`<span>` markup with our own classes.** Rejected: many extra elements per snippet, and the
  markup copied from the docs would carry presentational spans.
- **Prism or highlight.js classes (`.token.keyword`, `.hljs-keyword`).** Rejected: ties the
  system to one library's class names and its themes, which do not use our tokens.
- **Server-side highlighting with inline styles.** Rejected: literal colors bypass theming and
  the dark scheme.

### Prior art

- [CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-highlight-api-1/)
- [MDN: CSS Custom Highlight API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSS_Custom_Highlight_API),
  including its syntax highlighting example.
- [Prism](https://prismjs.com/) and [highlight.js](https://highlightjs.org/) token names, which
  the names above loosely follow.

### Open questions

- Should JS template literals and regular expressions get names of their own?

## Combobox (typeahead)

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/combobox.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as a web component over native markup.
CSS: [`css/components/molecules/combobox.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md) ·
Script: [`web-components/dui-combobox.js`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/dui-combobox.js) ·
Example: [`examples/molecules/combobox.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

Unlike the other explainers here, this pattern **has** an APG pattern: the
[APG Combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/), in its
[list autocomplete variant](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-autocomplete-list/).
This file records how domestic-ui maps it onto native HTML and the choices the APG leaves open.

### Problem

HTML can suggest values for a text field: an `<input list>` with a
[`<datalist>`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-datalist-element).
But the suggestion popup is drawn by the browser. It cannot be styled or themed, it looks and
filters differently in each engine and on mobile, it cannot show how many suggestions match, and
its support in assistive technology varies. Authors who need a consistent typeahead build one
from scratch, and many of those get the ARIA combobox contract wrong: focus moved into the list,
no `aria-expanded`, or results that change silently.

### Use cases

- Picking a city, a carrier or a product from a known list, while still allowing free text.
- Searching a long list held by a server: the page loads matching options as the user types.
- Filling a form field from suggestions, then submitting the form as usual.

### Goals

- The same markup works with JavaScript off, as a native `<input list>`.
- After the upgrade it follows the APG list autocomplete combobox exactly: focus stays in the
  input, the active option is conveyed with `aria-activedescendant`.
- The value is the input's value: forms, labels, `name` and validation do not change.
- Screen reader users hear how many options match after typing.
- Works at 320px wide, with targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels at every density.
- No fetch code inside the component; the page decides where options come from.

### Non-goals

- Select-only comboboxes, where the value must be one of the options: use `<select>`.
- Inline autocomplete (the rest of the top match typed into the input, `aria-autocomplete="both"`).
- Multiple values, grouped options, or rich option content.
- Fuzzy matching and ranking.

### Proposed markup and API

- The component MUST wrap a `<label>`, an `<input list="id">` and the `<datalist id="id">` it
  points to. **Our choice:** `<input list>` + `<datalist>` as the native fallback, not `<select>`,
  because the value is free text and the upgrade reuses the same input and the same options.
- The input MUST have an accessible name from its `<label>`. It SHOULD be the last visible child
  of `<dui-combobox>`: put hints and errors after the component and point at them with
  `aria-describedby`.
- Each `<option value>` in the datalist is a suggestion. An option MAY have a `label` that is
  shown as a hint after the value; filtering matches both.
- On upgrade the component MUST keep the same `<input>` element, MUST remove its `list`
  attribute (so the native popup never shows beside the listbox) and MUST add `role="combobox"`,
  `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `autocomplete="off"`.
- It MUST build a `<ul role="listbox">` after the input, labelled by the same `<label>`, with one
  `<li role="option">` per option, and a visually hidden `role="status"` region that exists from the
  upgrade on, before it is first updated.
- Filtering is built in. **Our choice:** case-insensitive "contains", not "starts with", because
  users often remember a word from the middle ("York" for "New York"), and the native datalist
  popups in Chromium and Firefox match the same way.
- On every `input` the component MUST dispatch `dui-combobox-filter` on itself (bubbles, cancelable,
  `detail: { query }`). A page that loads options itself MUST cancel it, then replace the options
  with `element.setOptions(values)` (strings or `{ value, label }` objects) or by changing the
  datalist's children; the component watches the datalist and re-reads it. While the event is
  canceled the component shows the options as given, unfiltered.
- When an option is accepted the component MUST set the input's value and dispatch `change` on the
  input, so forms and frameworks see the new value.
- The status region SHOULD say "N results", "1 result" or "No results" once typing pauses
  (400ms), not on every keystroke.
- **Our choice:** the listbox is absolutely positioned under the input inside `<dui-combobox>`,
  not a popover in the top layer. It is exactly as wide as the field, so it never overflows the
  viewport sideways, and it needs neither anchor positioning nor the popover fallback that
  centers a panel at the bottom of the viewport. The cost: an ancestor that clips its overflow also
  clips the list.

```html
<dui-combobox>
  <label for="city">City</label>
  <input type="text" id="city" name="city" list="city-options">
  <datalist id="city-options">
    <option value="Amsterdam"></option>
    <option value="Berlin"></option>
    <option value="Copenhagen"></option>
  </datalist>
</dui-combobox>
<script type="module" src="web-components/dui-combobox.js"></script>
```

Options from a server:

```js
combobox.addEventListener("dui-combobox-filter", async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const response = await fetch(`/cities?q=${encodeURIComponent(event.detail.query)}`);
  combobox.setOptions(await response.json());
});
```

Visuals: the list sits at the popover elevation and fades and grows in like a popover (the zoom is
dropped under reduced motion; every duration is `0s` with `data-motion="none"`). The active option
has an outline in the focus color and a tint, so it is not shown by color alone. Option heights
follow [density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/density.md).

### Keyboard interaction

Focus stays in the input throughout.

- Down Arrow: opens the list and moves to the next option (the first if none); wraps from last to first.
- Up Arrow: opens the list and moves to the previous option (the last if none); wraps from first to last.
- Alt+Down Arrow: opens the list without moving to an option. Alt+Up Arrow closes it.
- Enter: accepts the active option and closes the list. With no active option it does nothing
  special, so it submits the form.
- Escape: closes the list; if it is already closed, clears the input (as in the APG example).
  An empty, closed combobox lets Escape through, so a surrounding dialog still closes.
- Home / End: move the caret to the start or end of the input, and the list loses its active
  option. **Our choice:** follow the APG for editable comboboxes, where Home and End belong to the
  text field ("returns focus to the combobox and places the cursor"), rather than jumping to the
  first or last option, because the input is free text and the caret keys must keep working.
  Left and Right Arrow do the same.
- Typing: filters the options and opens the list when any match.
- Tab: accepts nothing, closes the list and moves on.
- Pointer: clicking an option accepts it; focus stays in the input.

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name / state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<input>` | `combobox` | From its `<label>`; `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant` while an option is active |
| `<ul>` | `listbox` | The same label (`aria-labelledby`) |
| `<li>` | `option` | Its value, plus the hint; `aria-selected="true"` on the active option |
| `<p class="visually-hidden">` | `status` | "5 results", polite ([WCAG 4.1.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)) |

A screen reader user hears, for example, "City, combobox, collapsed, editable", then after typing
"ber": "2 results", and on Down Arrow "Berlin, 1 of 2". Following the APG example, `aria-selected`
marks the option with visual focus; once accepted, the value lives in the input.

### Alternatives considered

- **`<datalist>` alone.** Kept as the no-script fallback. Rejected as the whole answer: the popup
  cannot be styled, differs between engines, gives no result count and is unreliable with some
  assistive technology.
- **`<select>` as the fallback.** Rejected: a select allows only its options and its enhanced form
  would be a select-only combobox; this pattern is free text with suggestions. Use `<select>` when
  the value must be one of a fixed set.
- **Customizable select (`appearance: base-select`).** The
  [customizable select](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Forms/Customizable_select)
  work ([`appearance`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/appearance),
  [Open UI explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/customizable-select.explainer/)) makes the
  `<select>` popup stylable. It is not interoperable yet, and it is still a select: no free text and
  no typing to filter. When it ships everywhere it is the answer for select-only comboboxes.
- **Open UI combobox research.** The [Open UI combobox explainer](https://open-ui.org/components/combobox.explainer/)
  explores a native, stylable combobox element. Nothing has shipped; we follow its direction (a
  native input plus options in the DOM) so a future element can replace the component.
- **Moving DOM focus into the list.** Rejected: the APG list autocomplete pattern keeps focus in
  the input so typing can continue; `aria-activedescendant` conveys the active option.
- **A popover in the top layer.** Rejected for now; see Our choice above.

### Prior art

- [APG Combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) and its
  [editable combobox with list autocomplete example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-autocomplete-list/).
- [GOV.UK accessible-autocomplete](https://github.com/alphagov/accessible-autocomplete).
- [Adrian Roselli: Under-Engineered Comboboxen?](https://adrianroselli.com/2023/06/under-engineered-comboboxen.html),
  on how far native `<datalist>` gets you.
- [MDN `combobox` role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/combobox_role)
  and [`aria-activedescendant`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-activedescendant).

### Mapping to a future standard

The contract is "a text input with a list of suggestions it owns". The markup is already the
native one (`<input list>` and `<datalist>`), so if browsers make the datalist popup stylable and
accessible, or ship the combobox element Open UI is researching, removing the `<dui-combobox>`
wrapper and its script is all a page needs to do.

### Open questions

- Should the list flip above the input near the bottom of the viewport? That needs anchor
  positioning (inside `@supports`) or a popover in the top layer.
- Should matching text in each option be marked, for example with `<mark>`?
- Should the component set `aria-busy` on the listbox while the page loads options?
- Should a select-only combobox wait for customizable `<select>` instead of a second component?

## Density

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/density.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as semantic tokens and one attribute.
CSS: the density tokens in [`css/tokens/semantic.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md) (sections 2 and 4) ·
Example: [`examples/patterns/density.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Data-heavy screens (tables, admin forms, toolbars) need to show more on one screen than a
marketing page or a settings form does. There is no web standard for density: no media query, no
user preference, no HTML attribute. Design systems invent their own, often a second set of
components or a scaled-down copy of the whole UI, and many make compact controls smaller than
people can reliably hit, or shrink the text with them.

### Use cases

- An order table with a filter form and a toolbar above it, where comfortable spacing shows ten
  rows and compact shows fifteen.
- An app shell whose main area is compact while a settings dialog inside it stays comfortable.
- A theme that makes controls a little taller everywhere, with compact following it.

### Goals

- One attribute on any element; everything inside follows, including nested components.
- Density changes space only: control heights, padding, gaps and table cells. Text size never
  changes ([WCAG 1.4.4](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html) is about
  the user's text size, which density must not fight).
- Compact keeps every target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels
  ([WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).
- Comfortable is the default; no attribute means comfortable.
- Plain CSS custom properties; themes can retune it.

### Non-goals

- A user-facing density preference. A page MAY offer one and set the attribute itself.
- Changing type sizes, icon sizes or layout (columns, breakpoints).
- More than two named levels.

### Proposed markup and API

- `data-density="compact"` on any element MUST tighten every component inside it.
  `data-density="comfortable"` MUST restore the default values inside a compact area.
- **Our choice:** an attribute on any ancestor, not a media query, because density follows the
  task (a data table, a toolbar), not the device or the viewport, and parts of one page often need
  different densities.
- The attribute sets one knob, `--dui-density-scale`: `1` comfortable, `0` compact. Components never
  read the knob. They read density-aware semantic tokens derived from it:

  | Token | Comfortable | Compact | Used by |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `--dui-size-control` | 44px (`--dui-size-target`) | 32px (`--dui-size-target-small`) | min block size of inputs, selects, buttons, check labels, summaries, tabs, nav, menu, pagination and listbox items |
  | `--dui-space-control-block` | 0.5rem | 0.25rem | block padding of the same |
  | `--dui-space-control-inline` | 0.75rem | 0.5rem | inline padding of text fields and items |
  | `--dui-space-button-inline` | 1rem | 0.75rem | inline padding of buttons and tabs |
  | `--dui-space-gap` | 0.5rem | 0.25rem | gap between the parts of a control |
  | `--dui-space-gap-tight` | 0.25rem | 0.125rem | gap and padding in groups: field, toolbar, pagination, menu |
  | `--dui-space-cell` | 0.5rem | 0.25rem | table cell padding |

- These tokens MUST be re-declared on every `[data-density]` element, as dependent tokens are on
  `[data-theme]` and `[data-motion]`: a custom property's `var()` references are resolved where it is
  declared ([CSS Variables, substitution](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-variables-1/#cycles)), so a
  token computed once on `:root` would not follow a knob changed lower down.
- Each token interpolates between its comfortable and compact value:
  `compact + (comfortable − compact) × --dui-density-scale`. A theme MAY set the knob between `0`
  and `1`; it MUST NOT go below `0`, which could take targets under 24px.
- Comfortable values come from other semantic tokens (`--dui-size-target`, the space scale), so a
  theme that changes them moves comfortable density with it.
- `small` and `large` buttons keep their sizes at every density.

```html
<main data-density="compact">
  <table>…</table>
  <dialog data-density="comfortable">…</dialog>
</main>
```

### Keyboard interaction

None. Density changes no behavior.

### Accessibility mappings

None: density is presentation only. It does not change roles, names or states, and it does not
change text size. Every interactive target stays at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels in compact (32px tall
controls; checkboxes, radios and switches are targeted through their 32px tall `<label>`).
`tests/density.spec.js` measures every control in the compact demo.

### Alternatives considered

- **A media query** (for example a viewport width or `pointer: coarse`). Rejected: density is a
  property of the content, not of the device, and a media query cannot give one part of a page a
  different density.
- **[`zoom`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/zoom) or scaling the root font size.**
  Rejected: both shrink text along with space, against the user's chosen text size, and scale
  targets proportionally, so a 44px control at `zoom: 0.5` would be 22px, under the WCAG 2.5.8
  minimum.
- **A second set of compact components** (`data-button="compact"` and the like on every component).
  Rejected: one attribute on an ancestor covers every component, including ones added later.
- **Separate compact tokens that authors swap by hand.** Rejected: nesting (comfortable inside
  compact) would need every token overridden twice.

### Prior art

- [Cloudscape Design System: Content density](https://cloudscape.design/foundation/visual-foundation/content-density/),
  which offers a comfortable and a compact mode.
- [WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- [MDN: Using CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Using_CSS_custom_properties)
  (inheritance and scoping).

### Mapping to a future standard

If a density user preference ever arrives as a media feature, a page would set
`data-density="compact"` on `:root` inside that media query; nothing else changes.

### Open questions

- Should compact also tighten the flow rhythm between blocks (`--dui-space-m`), or only space
  inside components, as now?
- Should there be a third, "spacious" level for touch-first screens?
- Should `small` buttons get smaller in compact, down to the 24px minimum?

## Drawer

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/drawer.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as a `<dialog>` variant.
CSS: [`css/components/molecules/dialog.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md) ·
Example: [`examples/molecules/dialog.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

A drawer (side sheet, off-canvas panel) slides in from an edge of the viewport to hold
filters, navigation or details. HTML has no drawer element and the APG has no drawer pattern.
Many implementations are a positioned `<div>` that does not trap focus, does not close on
Esc, leaves the page behind it reachable, and is hard-coded to the left or right edge.

### Use cases

- Filters for a list, next to the results.
- Site navigation on small screens.
- Details of a selected row, without leaving the table.

### Goals

- Everything a modal dialog does: focus moves in, the rest of the page is inert, Esc closes,
  focus returns to the opener.
- Start and end edges that follow the writing direction.
- Full block size of the viewport; the content scrolls with the header kept in view.
- An open and close transition that is off under reduced motion and harmless where unsupported.
- No JavaScript.

### Non-goals

- Swipe gestures.
- Drawers that push the page content aside.
- Top and bottom sheets.

### Proposed markup and API

- A drawer MUST be a `<dialog>` with `data-dialog="drawer"`, plus `start` or `end`
  (`end` is the default): `data-dialog="drawer start"`.
- It MUST have an accessible name, normally `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading.
- It SHOULD be opened with `showModal()` or `command="show-modal" commandfor="id"`, so it is modal.
- It MUST contain a visible way to close it: a `command="close"` button or a
  `<form method="dialog">` submit button.
- It MAY have `closedby="any"` so a click on the backdrop closes it. Where `closedby` is not
  supported, Esc and the close button still work.
- An optional `<header>` (heading and close button) stays at the top while the body scrolls;
  an optional `<footer>` holds actions.

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="filters" command="show-modal">Filters</button>
<dialog id="filters" data-dialog="drawer end" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="filters-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="filters-title">Filters</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="filters" command="close">Close</button>
  </header>
  <form method="dialog">
    …
    <footer><button type="submit">Apply</button></footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

**Our choice:** a drawer is a dialog variant, not a new element, because every behavior users
rely on (inertness, focus, Esc, the top layer) already comes with `<dialog>`.

### Keyboard interaction

- Enter / Space on the opener: opens the drawer and moves focus to its first focusable element
  (or the element with `autofocus`).
- Tab / Shift+Tab: move between focusable elements inside the drawer.
- Esc: closes the drawer and returns focus to the opener.

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name / state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` | `dialog`, modal | its heading, via `aria-labelledby` |
| Content outside | inert | not reachable |
| Close button | `button` | "Close" |

A screen reader user hears, for example, "Filters, dialog" and then the focused control. The
drawer's position is visual only; nothing about "start" or "end" is announced.

### Alternatives considered

- **A new `<dui-drawer>` element.** Rejected: it would re-implement focus trapping, inertness
  and Esc, all of which `<dialog>` already does correctly.
- **A `popover` element positioned at an edge.** Rejected as the default: a popover is not
  modal, so the page behind stays interactive and is not inert. It MAY be a reasonable
  non-modal drawer; see the open questions.
- **`left`/`right` keywords.** Rejected: they break in right-to-left languages. `start` and
  `end` follow [logical properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values).

### Prior art

- [WHATWG `dialog` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element)
  and [MDN `<dialog>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog),
  including `closedby`.
- [APG Dialog (Modal) pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).
- [MDN Invoker Commands API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API).
- [MDN `@starting-style`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style) and
  [`transition-behavior`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/transition-behavior).
- [WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html).

### Mapping to a future standard

The variant only changes position and motion. It could become a presentational hint on
`<dialog>` itself, or be expressed entirely in CSS with no attribute at all if a standard
"edge" placement for top-layer elements appears.

### Open questions

- Swipe to close on touch screens needs script; should a small component offer it?
- Non-modal drawers (a side panel that leaves the page usable): `dialog.show()` or a popover?
- Should a `start` drawer used for navigation be closed automatically when the viewport
  becomes wide enough to show the navigation inline?

## Pagination

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/explainers/pagination.html

Status: shipped in domestic-ui as a styling contract.
CSS: [`css/components/molecules/pagination.css`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md) ·
Example: [`examples/molecules/pagination.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md)

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are to be interpreted as described in
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)
when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

### Problem

Long lists and search results are split into pages. HTML has `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"`,
and ARIA has `aria-current="page"`, but there is no pagination element and no APG pattern
that says how to combine them. Common implementations announce bare numbers ("link, 5"),
use buttons for navigation, or leave a disabled "Previous" link that still receives focus
and goes nowhere.

### Use cases

- Search results with ten pages.
- An archive with hundreds of pages, where only nearby page numbers are shown.
- A table of records loaded one page at a time from the server.

### Goals

- Works with plain links and server rendering. No JavaScript.
- Every link has a complete accessible name ("Page 5", "Next page").
- The current page is announced as current, and looks different by more than color.
- Disabled ends are not focusable and not announced as links.
- Targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.

### Non-goals

- Deciding which page numbers to show (that is server logic).
- "Load more" buttons and infinite scroll.
- Client-side paging of a table already in the page.

### Proposed markup and API

- The container MUST be a `<nav>` with `data-pagination` and an `aria-label`. The label
  SHOULD be "Pagination", and MUST differ when a page has more than one pagination.
- Pages MUST be a list (`<ul>` or `<ol>`) of `<li>` items, each with one `<a href>`.
- Number links MUST have an accessible name that includes "Page", for example with a
  visually hidden "Page " before the number.
- The current page link MUST have `aria-current="page"`. **Our choice:** it stays a link, so it
  is announced in place and the list count does not change between pages.
- Previous and Next links SHOULD have `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"`, and MUST say "page" in their
  accessible name.
- At the first or last page, Previous or Next MUST be an `<a>` without `href` (a
  [placeholder link](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)).
  It is not focusable and has no link role. **Our choice:** keep it visible, so the row does not
  shift between pages.
- A gap in the numbers MAY be `<li aria-hidden="true">…</li>`.

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination" data-pagination>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="?page=4" rel="prev">Previous<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>1</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=5" aria-current="page"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>5</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>6</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6" rel="next">Next<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

Visuals: links are outlined boxes; the current page is filled with the accent color and bold,
with an inner focus ring in its text color; a disabled end has muted text (still 4.5:1) and a
dashed border.

### Keyboard interaction

- Tab: moves to the next page link / Shift+Tab: previous. Disabled ends are skipped.
- Enter: follows the focused link.

No arrow-key behavior: this is a list of links, not a composite widget.

### Accessibility mappings

| Element | Role | Name / state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<nav aria-label>` | `navigation` | "Pagination" |
| `<ul>` | `list` | item count |
| `<a href>` | `link` | "Page 4", "Previous page" |
| Current `<a>` | `link`, `aria-current="page"` | "Page 5, current page" |
| `<a>` without `href` | none (generic) | text only, not focusable |
| Gap `<li aria-hidden="true">` | hidden | not announced |

A screen reader user hears, for example, "Pagination, navigation, list, 6 items, link, Page 5,
current page".

### Alternatives considered

- **Buttons instead of links.** Rejected: pages are URLs. Links can be opened in a new tab,
  bookmarked and crawled, and need no script.
- **The current page as plain text.** A valid choice (some systems do it). Rejected as the
  default because the item is then announced without "link", and users who navigate by links
  skip it.
